Our cost-based extension places the economic value of advance commitment in the objective rather than prescribing revision budgets; our scenario-adaptive extension adapts revision timing to revealed information. For station-use minimization, we establish a cost decomposition across commitment intervals, yielding an exact dynamic program that reuses station subproblem solutions across model variants and parameter settings. As a more general alternative, we develop an integer L-shaped method strengthened by monotonicity-based cuts for budgeted formulations and enhanced cuts exploiting this decomposition. On automotive instances, including scenario trees with nearly 10,000 nodes, our combined model's average savings in expected station-use cost at the base-case discount reach 4.99% versus full adaptivity and 28.65% versus full commitment. Scenario adaptivity is most valuable when demand paths diverge and discounts justify commitment on some paths but not others, as in electrification-driven scenarios.
Counting Who Counts: Black Women Mathematicians in the United States
Olayemi Adeyemi; Ron Buckmire; Ranthony A. Clark; Shanzhen Gao; Jakini Kauba; Lakeshia Legette-Jones; Apoorva Mate; Omayra Ortega; José Pabón; Robin T. Wilson

For Black women in the mathematical sciences, histories have frequently been fragmented or omitted from official records, an absence that itself constitutes a form of exclusion. This project addresses this critical gap by constructing a curated dataset of 147 Black women who have earned doctoral degrees in mathematics and related mathematical sciences in the United States. By integrating archival research, institutional records, digital databases, and community knowledge, we establish a reproducible methodology for identifying, verifying, and documenting Black women mathematicians. We situate this dataset within a broader history of efforts to document Black mathematicians and describe how prior archival and community based initiatives informed its development. We then demonstrate the utility of the dataset through exploratory analyses of doctoral production, institutional pathways, undergraduate preparation, mentorship networks, and research areas. This revealed patterns including large concentrations of doctoral production among a small number of institutions and advisors. Additionally, our analysis highlights the vital role of Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) in preparing Black women who have earned doctoral degrees in the mathematical sciences. By transforming historical documentation into structured research infrastructure, this work provides a foundation for future investigations of mathematical communities using historical as well as mathematical, statistical, and computational methods. More broadly, the framework developed here offers a model for constructing datasets that support the study of underrepresented communities within the mathematical sciences.
The Projective Reed-Muller Code from Quartic Curves in the Projective Plane

We study the Hamming weight enumerator of the projective Reed-Muller code $\mathcal C_{2,4}$ over $\mathbf F_q$, with $\operatorname{char}(\mathbf F_q)>3$. We determine the geometrically reducible and singular contributions by combining incidence counts with counts of plane linear series on a fixed normalization. The line and conic configurations and the genus zero cases give explicit polynomials. The line-cubic and genus one cases give formulas involving class numbers. The genus two contribution is a finite sum over hyperelliptic models, using their point counts over $\mathbf F_q$ and $\mathbf F_{q^2}$ and their rational Weierstrass points. The remaining smooth contribution is the weighted point count distribution of nonhyperelliptic genus three curves.
A self-dual Dunkl wavelet frame and Besov--Triebel--Lizorkin spaces

We construct a self-dual Parseval wavelet frame associated with the Dunkl transform and use it to characterize the corresponding Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces for arbitrary smoothness and the full range of admissible indices. We also establish differential atomic decompositions with atoms supported on dilated Euclidean dyadic cubes, satisfying ordinary derivative estimates and polynomial moment indices. A key difficulty is the interaction between Euclidean dyadic cubes and the orbit geometry associated with the Dunkl operators. As applications, we obtain fractional chain rules and a Jackson inequality for nonlinear wavelet approximation in $L^p(dw)$.
Simple Strategy-Iteration with Dantzig's Rule is not Strongly Polynomial on Turn-Based Deterministic Games

We study turn-based deterministic zero-sum games with discounted and long-run average costs. For discounted costs, we establish exponential and superpolynomial iteration lower bounds for the simple strategy-iteration method with Dantzig's rule under unrestricted costs and unit weights, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this shows for the first time that the method is not strongly polynomial even when all action costs belong to $\{-1,0,1\}$. For long-run average costs, we establish an exponential iteration lower bound for termination of a Dantzig counterpart with unrestricted costs and prove that it admits a strongly polynomial implementation with unit weights.
Sharp estimates for imaginary powers of discrete Laplacians
The Anh Bui; The Quan Bui; Thanh Tinh Cao

Let $Δ_{\rm d}$ be the nonnegative discrete Laplacian on $\mathbb Z^d$. We prove that, for $0<p\le1$, \[ \|Δ_{\rm d}^{iγ}\|_{H^p_{Δ_{\rm d}}\to H^p_{Δ_{\rm d}}} \simeq (1+|γ|)^{d(1/p-1/2)}, \] and, for $1<p<\infty$, \[ \|Δ_{\rm d}^{iγ}\|_{\ell^p\to\ell^p} \simeq (1+|γ|)^{d|1/p-1/2|}. \] The estimates are sharp with respect to the exponent of $1+|γ|$. We also explain why the general spectral multiplier theorem and the usual Calderón--Zygmund approach do not give the sharp power.

A bridge splitting of a knot is weakly reducible if it has a pair of disjoint shadows, one from above and one from below, in the splitting surface. The process of weak reduction exchanges local minima and maxima in the splitting, untelescoping the splitting and giving a method for detecting essential surfaces in the knot complement. Bridge trisections generalize bridge splittings to the setting of surfaces in 4-manifolds. We define weak reducibility in this context, giving diagrammatic conditions for carrying out a weak reduction operation on bridge splittings. We produce a partial classification of 4-bridge trisections of surfaces in $S^4$.
Optimal global well-posedness for semilinear heat equations
Gael Y. Diebou; Nguyen Cong Phuc

We address the question of global in time existence for the semilinear parabolic equation \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{array}{rcl} \partial_t u-Δu&=&|u|^{b-1}u \quad {\rm ~in~} \mathbb{R}^n\times (0,\infty),\\ u(\cdot,0)&=& u_0 \quad {\rm ~in~} \mathbb{R}^n, \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} where $b> 1+2/n, n\geq 1$. We found a space of initial data $Z$ that guarantees the existence of a global in time solution whenever the norm of the initial datum $u_0$ in $Z$ is small. The space $Z$ is optimal in the sense that if $u_0$ is a nonnegative distribution and the equation admits a nonnegative solution $u\in L^b_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty))$, then $u_0\in Z$. Moreover, our result contains all of the known results in the literature. In particular, it implies that global in time existence does hold for end-point Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces, which resolves an open problem posed by L. Brandolese and F. Cortez (J. Funct. Anal. $\textbf{276}$ (2019), 2589-2604).
Quantum-Classical Hybrid Methods for Optimization: Lessons from Classical Decomposition

Quantum and physics-inspired solvers provide specialized sampling interfaces for Ising and quadratic unconstrained binary optimization models, but constrained optimization requires broader coordination and certification. This survey uses classical decomposition to analyze how such solvers can be integrated into hybrid quantum-classical algorithms. We distinguish formal decomposition, reformulation and reduction, and computational orchestration. For each interface, we ask what the transformation preserves, which assumptions make the outer method converge, and which certificates the implemented inner routine supplies. The central questions are whether that information meets the classical algorithm's requirements and whether hybridization improves solution quality or total cost enough to justify its coordination overhead. Benders decomposition, column generation, graph reduction, and copositive methods illustrate this distinction by separating heuristic proposals from classical certification. We also distinguish component effects within a fixed wrapper, reduction--solver interactions, and comparisons between complete quantum-enabled and classical systems. The analyzed studies provide conditional component benefits and favorable co-design evidence, but do not establish transferable end-to-end superiority over strong classical comparators. The resulting framework identifies opportunities for constraint programming and operations research in structure-preserving design, safeguarded hybrid algorithms, and controlled benchmarking.
Two routes to the Hadamard condition

In quantum field theory on curved spacetime, the Hadamard condition is often presented as a necessary condition on 'physically reasonable', 'vacuum-like' states of linear quantum fields, and plays a central role in many theoretical and foundational applications - ranging from proofs of the renormalizability of Wick polynomials to derivations of the Hawking temperature. In this paper, I strengthen, generalise, and bring under technical control two popular motivations for the Hadamard condition - one which appeals to the role of Hadamard states in defining physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator on general curved spacetime backgrounds, and one which appeals to the equivalence principle. This clarifies the role and status of the Hadamard condition, including its relationship to the equivalence principle, to well-definedness of physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator, and the sense in which Hadamard states are 'vacuum-like'.
Continuous and Differentiable Neural Network Representations of the Surfzone Sea-Surface from Lidar Point Clouds
David R. Culver; Matthias Morzfeld; Falk Feddersen

Ocean waves are often analyzed via sea-surface observations. Multi-beam scanning lidar enables two-dimensional measurements of the water surface $η(x,y)$ via sequenced point clouds of sea-surface elevation. Point cloud data, however, have to be gridded, interpolated, or mapped for use in wave analysis. We present and test a method for creating a continuous and differentiable (space and time), but grid-free, representation of the sea-surface from time sequenced lidar point clouds. We use a specific neural network architecture, a SIREN, to represent the sea-surface and to train the network on spatiotemporal 60~s of lidar data collected by a gas-electric UAS (drone) hovering over large (4 m), breaking waves in Monterey, California. The trained SIREN allows estimation of the sea-surface and its derivatives at any location and time. SIREN sea-surface representations tend to filter the highest wave number variability (splash-up and sea-spray). SIREN errors are comparable to instrument errors and insensitive to local data density. The reliability and reproducibility of our approach is tested by training two SIRENs independently on the same data. Differences between the two independent SIRENs are comparable to instrument error, but increase in data-poor regions. SIRENs' potential for directional wave analysis is demonstrated by computing spatial and temporal derivatives and by estimating wave velocity from a SIREN-generated space-time slice of the sea-surface.
Diagonal and branchwise criteria for universal Fourier series

We characterize diagonal profiles admitting universal real trigonometric Fourier series with factors in $\mathcal E_s=\bigcap_{p>s}\ell^p$ and $\ell^{s,q}$, $2\le s<\infty$, $1\le q\le\infty$. For nonincreasing profiles we obtain exact dyadic criteria and logarithmic endpoints. For independently regular odd/even sine/cosine branches we characterize simultaneous subseries, sign, and rearrangement universality for finite almost-everywhere targets. One function in every $L^p$, $1\le p<2$, supplies the coefficients. A separation example admits this realization although every compatible nonincreasing majorant with bounded relative cost belongs to $\ell^1$. Residue-class decompositions extend the criterion; a weakest-model condition permits extended-real rearrangement targets. A Walsh--Paley analogue gives the same diagonal tests for ternary modifications. Trigonometric realization uses Pogosyan's majorant theorem; the multiplier, factorization, projection-transfer, separation, and Walsh Fourier-origin arguments are proved here.
Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
Ricardo Freire; Cristian González-Riquelme; Claudio Muñoz; Felipe Poblete; Vicente Salinas

Let $χ_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,χ_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $ξ_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R,$ we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2}\, Φ_L(u)\, e^{izu}\, du, \] where $Φ_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ Φ_L(u) := \frac{1}{2π}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} ξ_L\!\left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu}\, ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $ξ_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $Λ_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge Λ_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $Λ_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $Λ_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $Λ_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $Λ_L\le953/3200=0.2978125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH by Platt and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.
Monomial Moving Zeros for the Heat Semigroup: An Explicit Finite-Order Differential Hierarchy

Let $P_t=\exp(t\D^2/2)$ be the heat semigroup. For every integer $k\geq2$ and parameter $ρ\in\C$, we construct an entire function $Γ_{ρ,k}$ whose heat evolution has the prescribed moving zero $x=ρt^k$ and constant spatial flux there: \[ (P_tΓ_{ρ,k})(ρt^k)=0, \qquad \partial_x(P_tΓ_{ρ,k})(ρt^k)=1. \] The initial function is explicit, \[ Γ_{ρ,k}(x) =x\sum_{q\geq0}\frac{(-2^kρx^{2k-1})^q}{q!} \frac{(kq)!}{((2k-1)q+1)!}, \] and is a generalized hypergeometric function whose entire-function order is strictly below two. Most importantly, it is annihilated by an explicit polynomial-coefficient differential operator of order $2k-1$. Thus every monomial moving boundary admits a finite-order stationary realization after a natural boundary-flux selection, even though the naive order-$k$ family $\D^k+a x^{k-1}$ already fails to produce the exact boundary at $k=4$. No minimality claim is made: the result gives a universal finite-order hierarchy, while the least possible differential order remains open and depends on the choice made inside the inverse kernel.
Michael Rabin's fingerprints across the theory of computation

Michael O. Rabin was a major founder and leader of theoretical computer science. He died on April 14, 2026, at the age of 94. This paper aims to survey the wide scope and lasting impact of his research.
Alexander Grigor'yan; Leandro F. Pessoa; Alberto G. Setti

We describe the $L^p$-parabolicity of a Riemannian manifold in terms of a unified theory of nonlinear $L^p$-capacities, for the whole range $1\leq p\leq \infty$. For example, the \(L^{1}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to the usual notion of parabolicity/recurrence, while \(L^{2}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to biparabolicity. For any $1\leq p\leq \infty,$ the $L^p$-parabolicity turns out to be equivalent to the $L^q$-Liouville property for positive superharmonic functions, where $p$ and $q$ are Hölder conjugate exponents. We also provide a new capacitary characterization of the $L^1$-Liouville property. Finally we obtain an almost optimal volume growth condition for the $L^p$-parabolicity for $1<p\leq 2$ as well as a sharp volume condition for all $1<p<\infty$ for manifolds of non-negative Ricci curvature and for model manifolds.
The algebraic and geometric classification of $3$-Poisson algebras
Hani Abdelwahab; Kobiljon Abdurasulov; Ivan Kaygorodov

$3$-Poisson (ternary Nambu--Poisson) algebras are the algebras of observables of Nambu mechanics, the generalization of Hamiltonian mechanics in which the time evolution $\dot f=\{f,H_1,H_2\}$ is governed by two Hamiltonians and preserves the phase volume; their $3$-Lie part also gives the gauge algebra of the Bagger--Lambert--Gustavsson model of multiple M2-branes. We give the algebraic classification of complex $4$-dimensional $3$-Poisson algebras (seven algebras) and of complex $5$-dimensional nilpotent $3$-Poisson algebras ($38$ algebras and one one-parameter family) with both multiplications non-zero. We also describe the algebraic counterpart of the Inönü--Wigner contractions of physics: the variety of complex $4$-dimensional $3$-Poisson algebras has dimension $16$ and seven irreducible components, one of which is the orbit closure of the simple $3$-Lie algebra of the M2-brane model, and the variety of complex $5$-dimensional nilpotent $3$-Poisson algebras has dimension $20$ and five irreducible components.
Chaotic CLT using Poisson Fourth Moment Theorem and Graph Theory

In this article, we consider the parabolic Anderson model and the hyperbolic Anderson model in dimension 1, driven by a time-independent Lévy noise, which is either white, or colored with integrable coloration kernel $κ$. Using a Poisson version of the Fourth Moment Theorem due to Döbler, Vidotto and Zheng (2018), we prove that the spatial integral of the solution satisfies a central limit theorem. We prove that this result also holds for the hyperbolic Anderson model in dimension $d=2$, if in addition $κ$ is bounded. To estimate the fourth cumulant of the projection of the spatial integral on a fixed chaos, we develop a novel technique using graph theory, which allows us to handle some intricate integrals involving the modified contractions.
Counterexamples to the total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture

The total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture asserts that the ground-state particle density and total current determine the scalar potential up to an additive constant and the vector potential up to a gauge transformation. We give three counterexamples for two spinless fermions in the physically relevant setting of three spatial dimensions. In each, a Hamiltonian $H^{v,\mathbf{A}}$ has a nondegenerate ground state with identically zero total current but nonzero magnetic field. Complex conjugation then yields a second Hamiltonian $H^{v,-\mathbf{A}}$, with the same scalar potential and interaction, whose ground state has the same density and the same zero current, while the magnetic field is reversed. The first two examples are noninteracting. One is explicit, with a smooth bounded vector potential and a Gaussian density. The other has smooth bounded scalar and vector potentials in the standard potential spaces. The third example has Coulomb repulsion with unit coupling, an isotropic harmonic scalar potential, and Dirac monopole fields of magnetic charge $\pm 1/2$. The monopole example uses vector potentials defined on separate spatial patches, since these fields are not curls of globally defined smooth vector potentials.
Graphexon Mean Field Games on Large Network Limits

This paper analyzes graphexon mean field games (GXMFG) on large network limits. By considering edge distributions of a sequence of finite graphs, we define the empirical graphexon measures and study their subsequential weak limits in a graphexon space consisting of all symmetric probability measures on $[0,1]^{2d}$. This concept of network limits extends graphon theory to general, not necessarily dense, networks. To formulate the game using the graphexon limit, we exploit a useful property that a probability measure on a product space is the product of a probability kernel and a marginal distribution. Based on such graph limits and the probability kernel of the associated graphexon measure, we derive the GXMFG equations, and present a detailed analysis for the linear-quadratic case. For linear-quadratic models with finite populations residing over large networks, we use the GXMFG equations to construct decentralized strategies, for which an $ε$-Nash equilibrium property is established.
PL standardness of the four-pentachoron census sphere Q

We prove that the four-pentachoron homotopy \(4\)-sphere \(Q\) singled out in the census of Burke, Burton and Spreer is PL homeomorphic to the standard \(4\)-sphere. The key construction identifies the compact exterior of an explicit locally flat \(2\)-sphere in an auxiliary 39-vertex model of \(Q\) with the exterior of Budney, Burton and Hillman, then certifies its fibration by a normal cut followed by a relative collapse. The exterior identification uses finite checked moves, an exact regular-neighbourhood construction and a PL lemma controlling the passage through an ideal triangulation. Cutting the compact exterior along the specified normal hypersurface gives a manifold that collapses onto one boundary copy of the punctured \(3\)-torus in 209,144 elementary pairs; a marked product lemma identifies the cut as a product. The resulting integral monodromy realizes \(Q\) as a Cappell--Shaneson filling whose two surgery framings are standard by Gompf's results. The fibration certificate is independent of Issa's earlier PL-compatible constructions. Combined with the published census, the result establishes standardness for every homotopy \(4\)-sphere triangulated with at most four pentachora.
Explicit sharp gradient stability of the $L^{p}$-Poincaré inequality and fundamental gaps for the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian operator

In this paper, we prove the gradient stability of the $L^{p}$-Poincaré inequality with explicit constants on bounded convex domains for any $1<p<\infty$. These estimates control the distance to the optimizers in the strongest possible norm with the optimal stability exponent $\max\{2,p\}$, exhibiting the same phenomenon initially observed by Figalli and Zhang [FZ22a] for the $L^p$-Sobolev inequality. As a result, we also confirm the conjecture posed by Fleckinger-Pellé and Takáč [FPT02, Section 8]. We then apply the inequality to obtain positive fundamental gap estimates in terms of the inradius for the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian.
A Pittel-type limit law for the largest component of random $d$-uniform hypergraphs: enumeration and excursions

Let $H_d(n,M)$ be a $d$-uniform hypergraph with $n$ vertices and $M$ hyperedges. In the critical window $M=\frac{n}{d(d-1)}(1+λn^{-1/3})+O(1)$, its largest component $L_n$ satisfies $$n^{-2/3}L_n\xrightarrow{\mathcal L} \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Pit}}\bigl((d-1)^{1/3}a,λ(d-1)^{-2/3}\bigr).$$ (Here $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Pit}}(x,μ)$ denotes the limiting law of the largest component of the critical random graph established by Pittel (2001).) The proof rests on two pillars. First, a bivariate exponential formula gives the exact finite-size law of $L_n$. Subsequently, cancellation of the orders $n,n^{2/3},n^{1/3}$ in the tree normalization determines the series of rooted hypertrees, then that of unicyclic components and its singular expansions at the radius of convergence $ρ_d$. These calculations are exact; they serve the fixed-excess identities and the cancellation mechanism, and nothing more: no unproved uniformity in the excess enters the proof of the limit law. Next, by exploration and martingale approximation, the ordered sizes converge unconditionally to the excursion lengths of a Brownian motion with parabolic drift. A monotone coupling transfers the law to $H_d(n,M)$. The limit law is then identified with Pittel's law by a Brownian rescaling: if $h=d-1$, it suffices to multiply lengths by $h^{-1/3}$ and evaluate at parameter $λh^{-2/3}$. The exact Poisson representation dispenses with any separate deconditioning. We also formulate a two-regime $d$-uniform Bollobas bound (Wright for fixed $\ell$, global combinatorial beyond that), and explicitly indicate why neither regime alone suffices to close the analytic route.
Analytical solution of electromagnetic heating in a stratified absorbing medium

We consider the temperature evolution in a skin tissue when it is exposed to an electromagnetic wave. The heating is caused by the absorbed power as the electromagnetic wave attenuates inside the skin. In many applications, the characteristic depth of attenuation is small in comparison with the lateral size of the electromagnetic beam. Because of this separation of length scales, the lateral heat conduction is negligible at leading order. Previously, we studied electromagnetic heating in a skin of a single homogeneous layer. We derived the leading-term analytical solution and the asymptotic corrections up to the second order for lateral heat conduction and for oblique incidence. In this study, we derive the analytical solution in the case of perpendicular incidence on a stratified skin tissue with a layer-specific profile for electromagnetic attenuation. It should be emphasized that in the current study, the heat capacity and conductivity are still uniform over the entire skin tissue; only the electromagnetic attenuation is stratified resulting in a layer-specific heating profile.
Ordered frequency in relatively hyperbolic groups

We study word frequencies along infinite strings whose finite prefixes lie in a regular language of geodesic representatives of group elements. Let \((G,\mathcal H)\) be a non-elementary relatively hyperbolic pair, and suppose that, over a finite symmetric generating set, there is a prefix-closed regular language containing exactly one shortest word representing each element of \(G\). Modeling this language using a finite-state Markov chain, we define a probability measure on the space of infinite strings whose finite prefixes are words belonging to this language. Each such string labels a geodesic ray emanating from the identity. We show there is a continuous surjection from this space onto the Bowditch boundary, and the pushforward of the probability measure under this map is a Patterson--Sullivan probability obtained as a weak limit of weighted counts of group elements. For a word \(w\), the ordered frequency of \(w\) along a given labeled ray is the limiting proportion of consecutive nonoverlapping tuples of length \(|w|\) that exactly spell \(w\). For almost every infinite string under the constructed measure, these frequencies exist simultaneously for all nonempty geodesic words, with no restriction on their lengths. Consequently, almost every boundary point with respect to this Patterson--Sullivan probability is the endpoint of at least one such ray along which all these frequencies exist. In particular, after possibly enlarging the generating set, these results apply when the peripheral subgroups are virtually abelian.
The integral $K_0$-ring of the stack of smooth hyperelliptic curves

We compute the integral $K_0$-ring of the moduli stack $\mathscr H_g$ of smooth hyperelliptic curves of genus $g\ge2$ over a field of characteristic zero. We show that it is a free abelian group of rank $8g+2$ for even $g$ and $8g+4$ for odd $g$. We use the isotypic decomposition of the $K_0$ of a related $μ_{g+1}$-gerbe to obtain presentations for both even and odd $g$'s from the standard quotient presentation of $\mathscr H_g$. Thus, our technique differs from the $CH^\bullet(\mathscr H_g)$ computations of Edidin--Fulghesu, Fulghesu--Viviani, Di Lorenzo, and the $K_0(\mathscr M_2)$ computation of Edidin--Hu. Using Pagani's description of the inertia stack of $\mathscr H_g$, we apply Riemann--Roch to interpret the rank of $K_0(\mathscr H_g)$ as the number of inertia components. Finally, we compare the $K_0$ and Chow rings of $\mathscr H_g$ through the gamma-filtration and give presentations to the associated graded rings $\operatorname{gr}_γK_0(\mathscr H_g)\otimes\mathbb F_p$ for every prime $p$.
Solving the Ho--Nguyen Conjecture for Gaussian Mixtures: Applications to Mixtures of Experts

Over-fitted Gaussian mixtures can contain many parameter configurations with nearly the same density, making the order of density cancellation central to their parameter-learning rates. Ho and Nguyen encoded these cancellations in a polynomial system and conjectured its exact order as a function of cluster size. The key to resolving the conjecture is a common positive-variance shift that turns the coefficient equations into Gaussian moment matching. For every cluster size $\Mhn\ge2$, we prove that the real, nonzero-weight system has order $2\Mhn$: a sharp sign-change bound forces rigidity at that order, while positive Gauss--Hermite quadrature constructs a non-trivial solution through order $2\Mhn-1$. Population-density calculations at 110-digit working precision recover the predicted leading term for two to six components; finite multistart searches recover the same observed powers for two to five components, with smaller finite-scale constants for three to five components. For parameter learning, the exact order gives an explicit pointwise maximum-likelihood exponent and an exact local minimax order on specified shrinking neighbourhoods of a fixed known mixing measure. The same coefficient viewpoint separates high-order cancellation from exact parameter symmetries in mixtures of experts. Synchronized replication preserves the conditional density while keeping the corresponding parameter losses positive in two broad standard-softmax classes, showing why statistical rate arguments must account for exact parameter symmetries.
Andre M. Sonnet; Epifanio G. Virga

Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.
Convolution Quadrature with Adaptive History Compression for Variable-Order Fractional Reaction--Diffusion Equations

We develop a fully implicit fast method for semilinear variable-order fractional reaction--diffusion equations with periodic fractional diffusion and exponential-transition Scarpi memory. A Volterra-resolvent analysis establishes local well-posedness and temporal regularity estimates that describe the weak initial singularity. Backward Euler convolution quadrature combined with Fourier pseudospectral discretization achieves mesh-uniform stability and positive-time first-order convergence. To accelerate the scheme, we utilize Cauchy--FFT weight recovery and adaptive blockwise sum-of-exponentials compression, which significantly reduces the cost of history evaluation under local error control. A logarithmic perturbation bound quantifies the effects of weight recovery, history compression, and inexact nonlinear solves, giving tolerance conditions that preserve the convergence order. Numerical experiments confirm the first-order accuracy and demonstrate that the accelerated method efficiently resolves long-time spatial patterns at a substantially reduced computational cost.
From Hermite Chaos to an Attractive Log-Gas: Explicit High-Rank Limits of Iterated-Logarithm and Tail Constants

Let $Z$ be a standard Hermite process of order $m\ge2$ and Hurst index $H\in(1/2,1)$. For $d<H-1/2$, let $Y$ be the variance-normalized version of the weighted integral $\int_0^1 x^{-d}\,\mathrm dZ(x)$. Its right tail satisfies $ \log\Pr\{Y>t\}\sim -\frac12\left(\frac{t}{Λ_m}\right)^{2/m}, t\to\infty, $ where the positive constant $Λ_m$ admits an infinite-dimensional variational representation. The same constant governs the sharp law of the iterated logarithm for weighted sums of nonlinear functions of long-memory Gaussian sequences. A general closed-form evaluation at finite order is not known. As $m\to\infty$ with $H$ and $d$ fixed, the normalized constants $\sqrt{m!}\,Λ_m$ decrease to an explicit positive function of $H$ and $d$, with relative error $O(m^{-1})$. This function also gives a lower bound for the normalized constant at every finite order. An exact Rényi variational representation at each order yields, in the high-rank limit, the entropy--energy variational problem of an attractive logarithmic gas. The limiting free energy is evaluated through the Selberg integral and the Barnes $G$ function. For $d\le0$, convergence remains uniform up to the memory boundary $H=1/2$. After division by the square-root boundary factor $\sqrt{2H-1}$, the high-rank and boundary limits commute. Their common value is explicit; for constant weights it equals $2^{3/2}π^3G(1/2)^8=2^{11/6}πe\,\mathsf A^{-12}$, where $\mathsf A$ is the Glaisher--Kinkelin constant. The quadratic and cubic coefficients of the fixed-order expansion of the normalized constant as $H\uparrow1$ converge, as $m\to\infty$, to those of the explicit limiting function. Global finite-order bounds and a concentrating-weight limit complement the main result.
Quantum polynomial-time conjugacy in metabelian groups

We prove that the conjugacy problem in finitely presented metabelian groups with a fixed number of generators is solvable in bounded-error quantum polynomial time, uniformly in the defining relations of the group. Both the group presentation and the words representing the elements are part of the input. The main ingredient is a quantum polynomial-time algorithm for computing all multiplicative relations among a fixed number of units in a commutative affine $\mathbb Z$-algebra presented with a fixed number of variables. The algorithm reduces the problem to computations in finite-dimensional algebras over $\mathbb Q$ and finite rings by identifying the lattice of exponent vectors whose corresponding products are algebraic over the coefficient field. An effective arithmetic splitting combines the rational and finite-ring computations. The proof uses effective bounds for polynomial equations, algorithms for finite-dimensional commutative algebras, quantum integer factorization, and finite abelian hidden-subgroup algorithms.
On counterexamples to the unification of free entropy

It has been a long-standing open problem to determine when two versions of Voiculescu's free entropy, $χ$ and $χ^*$, agree. OpenAI recently generated the first example with $-\infty < χ< χ^*$. We give a detailed presentation of a similar example, and explicitly show the separation between free Fisher information and the large-$n$ limit of classical Fisher information through the relationship with Wasserstein distance. We thus situate the example in the context of probability theory and information geometry.
Combining Exponential and Polynomial Convergence Rates for Accelerated Extremum Seeking: A High-Order Lie Bracket Approach

In this paper, we leverage the recently developed general higher-order Lie bracket approximation theory and framework for control-affine systems to show that we can design extremum seeking (ES) systems that combine flows based on: (i) first-order Lie bracket approximation, which provide an exponential convergence rate for quadratic objective functions and polynomial convergence rate for non-quadratic objective functions; and (ii) higher-order Lie bracket approximation, which provide exponential convergence rate near the minimizer even if the objective function is non-quadratic (i.e., flatter and possesses vanishing Hessian at the minimizer). Such combination provides an accelerated ES design that benefits from the polynomial decay rate farther away from the minimizer and exponential decay rate near the minimizer even for complicated nature of objective functions. We provide numerical simulations to demonstrate the results, including multi-variable and nonpolynomial flat-bottomed objective functions.
Small sums of roots of unity: polylogarithmic exceptional sets and conditional separation

We prove a polylogarithmic exceptional-set estimate for symmetric five-term sums of roots of unity of arbitrary order. More precisely, at most $O((\log(2N))^{11})$ points of the $N$-grid satisfy $|1+2\cos(2πx)+2\cos(2πy)|<\exp(-C(\log(2N))^{13})$. This implies the corresponding bound for small conjugates at the reduced conductor: outside polylogarithmically many real embeddings, every such sum is at least quasipolynomially large. The proof is unconditional and combines a polynomial-vector-field multiplicity estimate, arithmetic jet determinants, analytic propagation, and interpolation determinants for nearby grid points. As a companion result, assuming a uniform number-field $abc$ conjecture, we prove that every sum of a fixed number of distinct prime-order roots of unity has modulus at least $\exp(-\varepsilon p)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, uniformly in the exponents. That proof uses simultaneous compression of the exponents, discriminant estimates, and cyclic resultants.
Connected $ω$-limit sets of Cournot maps: periodic orbits, realization and almost every point

Let $F(x,y)=(f_2(y),f_1(x))$ be a Cournot map of the unit square, $φ=f_2\circ f_1$ and $χ=f_1\circ f_2$. Linero Bas and Muñoz Guillermo proved that an $ω$-limit set of $F$ with nonempty interior is connected if and only if \textup{(C1)} its two projections are connected and \textup{(C2)} $ω_{F^2}(z)\capω_{F^2}(F(z))\neq\emptyset$, and conjectured that this holds for every $ω$-limit set. We prove the conjecture for every point $z=(x,y)$ such that $ω_φ(x)$ or $ω_χ(y)$ is finite, and for Lebesgue almost every point $z$ of the square whenever $φ$ is metrically regular (every metric attractor is a periodic orbit, a solenoid, or a cycle of intervals carrying a well-behaved absolutely continuous invariant measure). Over a periodic orbit the $ω$-limit set is a \emph{comb}, whose sections are rigid; when one projection is connected it is a point, a \emph{lattice} $(P\times J)\cup(K\times Q)$ with $P\subset K$, $Q\subset J$ and $\#P=\#Q$, or an \emph{alternating comb} of $2m$ disjoint segments. Conversely, every lattice and every alternating comb is an $ω$-limit set of a Cournot map with piecewise linear reaction functions; the construction rests on a lemma producing exact compositions of piecewise linear maps with prescribed values. This answers, for this class, the question of Balibrea, Linero and Cánovas of which nowhere dense sets are $ω$-limit sets of Cournot maps. For instance, the letter H is not an $ω$-limit set at any such point, and for metrically regular $φ$ the points whose $ω$-limit set is connected, infinite, nowhere dense and not a lattice form a Lebesgue null set.
A functional central limit theorem for the KPZ equation with narrow wedge initial data
Raluca M. Balan; Le Chen; Jinxin Wang

In this article, we consider the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation with narrow wedge initial data. We prove a functional central limit theorem for the spatial average of the solution, which solves an open problem from Gu and Pu (2025). Our main tool is Clark-Ocone formula from Malliavin calculus, combined with an in-depth analysis of the increments of the solution. The main step is a moment bound for time increments of the normalized spatial integral. For this, we introduce a new technique, called a ``common-ray'' change of variables. Using the fact that Malliavin derivative of the solution satisfies a Chapman-Kolmogorov relation, we reduce the kernel differences at two times to spatial increments at one common time.
Minimality and stability of the ball for the charge-qubit energy

We study the shape optimization problem introduced by Mazzoleni, Muratov, and Ruffini as a model for a superconducting charge qubit, in which the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of a set of prescribed volume competes with the Coulomb self-energy of the ground state. We prove that, for sufficiently small charge, the ball is the unique minimizer, and that the energy deficit of a volume-preserving and centered perturbation of the ball is comparable to the squared $H^{1/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, with constants independent of the charge. We also obtain the corresponding results for the quadratic Hartree--Ohta--Kawasaki model.
A Brezis--Merle inequality for the biharmonic operator with Dirichlet boundary conditions in four-dimensional balls
João Marcos do Ó; Federica Sani; Victor Rafael Silva

In this paper, we establish a Brezis-Merle type inequality for very weak solutions of the biharmonic Dirichlet problem in the four-dimensional unit ball. By combining this inequality with moving-plane arguments, we obtain uniform a priori estimates for positive solutions of semilinear biharmonic equations with exponential nonlinearities in both the subcritical and critical regimes. As an application of these estimates, we prove the existence of a positive solution by means of topological methods. We also extend the analysis to a class of non-variational cooperative systems.
DeGroot Dynamics on Multiplex Networks with Directed and Acyclic Interlayer Connectivities
Mia Zender; Kye Shi; Abigail Hickok; Weiqi Chu; Mason A. Porter

In models of opinion dynamics, researchers typically examine how an individual's opinion on one topic is influenced by the opinions of their neighbors in a network. However, people's opinions on a topic are also influenced by their opinions and their neighbors' opinions on related topics. In an election, for example, the opinions of a voter on a variety of issues inform their opinions of electoral candidates. To consider the influence between people's opinions on multiple distinct topics, we study a multiplex extension of the traditional DeGroot consensus model. In our multiplex DeGroot model, different network layers represent distinct topics and directed interlayer edges (which are not allowed to form cycles) encode relationships between distinct topics. In our model, an individual's opinion on one topic is influenced both by the opinions of their neighbors on that topic and by their own opinions on related topics. We prove under mild conditions that our multiplex DeGroot model converges to a limit state. We also prove that strong connectedness in ``source layers'' (which represent fundamental beliefs) eventually yields a consensus opinion in each layer. In particular, we show that consensus on source layers can lead to consensus on other layers even when those layers otherwise would be polarized. By numerically simulating our multiplex DeGroot model on a two-layer network, we examine the effects on opinion dynamics of (1) different network structures and (2) different types of initial opinion data.
Low Residuals, Wrong Value: Learning the Viscosity Solution of Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs Equations with PINNs
Raul Jimenez; Pablo Tejerina-Pérez; Leonid Sarieddine; Pedro Tarancón-Álvarez; Marisol Traforetti; Pau Solé-Vilaró; Oleksii Ignatenko; Nazar Tkach; Pavlos Protopapas

Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and other residual-trained solvers judge a candidate solution by the size of its sampled PDE residual. For first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations this is not sufficient: the same equation and boundary data admit Lipschitz almost-everywhere solutions that differ from the viscosity solution by $O(1)$ while violating the equation only on sets of measure zero. We study whether residual minimization selects such solutions in a fixed-horizon pursuit-evasion game whose Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs value function is known in closed form on the circle $S^1$ and on the flat tori $\mathbb{T}^{2}$ and $\mathbb{T}^{4}$. We train four neural parameterizations with ten seeds on each geometry, 120 runs in total. A standard network with periodic Fourier features converges to folded almost-everywhere solutions in all 30 runs: small residuals and the expected capture-layer gradient, yet values that are wrong over most of the domain. A network with periodicity imposed through the loss recovers the viscosity solution in one and two dimensions but becomes unreliable in four. Two parameterizations that receive the geodesic distance do substantially better: a single network fed the wrapped displacement and its distance recovers the viscosity solution in all 30 runs, while a minimum over periodic image charts succeeds in 27 of 30 and introduces a wrong-image failure mode. Finally, for the convex Hamiltonian considered here, we use the semiconcavity of the viscosity solution to build a mesh-free finite-difference test that needs only forward network evaluations; it detects the folded solutions and the harmful min-of-charts failures without access to the exact value function. A small sampled residual thus does not by itself validate a learned Hamilton-Jacobi solution; the parameterization and independent structural diagnostics can be essential for selecting the viscosity solution.
Canard points in planar mass-action networks: a flux criterion, a duality, and a complete classification

We determine which mass-action reaction networks on two species, one fast and one slow, admit a canard point: a singular Hopf bifurcation at a fold of the critical manifold, followed by a canard explosion. In flux coordinates, existence reduces to three linear equations, one linear inequation and a sign condition on the product of two linear forms, and the criticality of the explosion is the sign of an explicit cubic form. For four reactions with a balance matrix of full rank, both become integer polynomial conditions on the stoichiometry. A vacancy duality, which exchanges the activator-inhibitor and substrate-depletion mechanisms, preserves canard points together with their criticality. The central structural result is a mode criterion: a network has a canard point if and only if its elementary flux modes contain a sign-meeting pair and a mode carrying a fold. Hence every canard network contains a minimal one carried by at most three modes, and so by at most twelve reactions, whatever the molecularity. For complexes of molecularity at most three we enumerate all 138,754 minimal canard networks and label each exactly by the criticalities it admits. None has more than six reactions; 32 have canard points of codimension zero and no explosion; and most six-reaction networks admit both criticalities, separated by degenerate canard points. All labels rest on exact certificates.
Geometry of a class of $φ$-minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^2\times \mathbb{R}$
Katianny Rosa Freitas; João Paulo dos Santos; António Martínez

We study a class of $φ$-minimal surfaces in the product space $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{R}$, that is, weighted minimal surfaces whose corresponding weight is determined by a smooth potential function $φ$ that depends only on the height coordinate relative to the factor $\mathbb{R}$. Under monotonicity, concavity, and asymptotic conditions on $φ$, we obtain a complete classification of connected, properly embedded $φ$-minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{R}$ acting trivially on $\mathbb{R}$ and by rotations or parabolic translations on $\mathbb{H}^2$. Finally, we establish several non-existence results for $φ$-minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^2 \times \mathbb{R}$, either by using properties of the height function or by applying the tangency principle together with suitable invariant surfaces as barriers.
Thomas Berger; Hannes Gernandt; Pushya Mitra

We analyze explicit and implicit Euler discretizations of the continuous-time closed-loop dynamics generated by a funnel controller for a fully actuated nonlinear full-state system of relative degree one with scalar positive input gain. A quantitative continuous-time funnel margin provides the compactness and regularity bounds needed for the error analysis. For explicit Euler, a computable upper step-size threshold guarantees a global nodewise distance from the funnel boundary. We show that first-order convergence holds on finite time horizons and, under a~dissipativity condition (a~one-sided Lipschitz bound on the plant dominated by the funnel damping), uniformly in time. For implicit Euler, an admissible update exists for every step size and every trajectory initialized in the funnel retains a step-size-independent nodal margin. Under dissipativity, the admissible root is unique for every step size, the discrete flow is contractive, and the first-order error bound is uniform in time.
Counterexamples to the Monotone Completeness Conjecture

Combining a modification of the recent counterexample to the quasitrace conjecture with model-theoretic reductions due to the first author, we exhibit a counterexample to the monotone completeness conjecture. We fully reproduce the disproof of the quasitrace conjecture by a modified construction and arguments.
Total $\{k\}$-domination in caterpillars: Structural properties and exact results
Mariana Escalante; Paola Tolomei; María Inés Lopez Pujato

The total $\{k\}$-domination problem ($T\{k\}DP$) seeks a minimum-weight function such that the sum of weights in every open neighborhood is at least $k$. While this problem is known to be NP-hard for general graphs, we demonstrate that for the family of caterpillars, it simplifies to the classical total domination number ($k=1$) via the identity $γ^{\{k\}}_t(G) = kγ_t(G)$. This reduction is supported by a general upper bound established for all graphs, which we prove to be tight specifically for caterpillars. The central tool for our analysis is the introduction of a $(T,R)$-representation, a one-to-one mapping that abstracts caterpillar structure into discrete vectors based on support vertex distribution and central path segment lengths. By characterizing these segments through congruence modulo 4, we derive an exact closed-form expression for the total $\{k\}$-domination number of any caterpillar graph.
Large Deviations in Stochastic Dynamics: A Hamiltonian Perspective
Lorenzo Cirigliano; William D. Piñeros; Anna Poggialini; Grant M. Rotskoff; Eric Vanden-Eijnden

These lecture notes present an introduction to large deviations in stochastic dynamical systems, adapted from a lecture series given at the Les Houches school ``Large Deviations: Theory and Applications'' in July 2024. The exposition develops the theory through a unified methodology: WKB analysis of backward Kolmogorov equations, which reveals the Hamiltonian structure underlying all large deviation principles considered here. We treat three asymptotic regimes systematically. First, the small-noise limit for stochastic differential equations and the large-volume limit for Markov jump processes, where the Large Deviation Principle emerges from the Law of Large Numbers through progressively finer characterizations of fluctuations. Second, the long-time limit combined with small noise, yielding the quasipotential formalism for metastability and transition rates in both equilibrium and nonequlibrium systems. Third, the long-time limit at finite noise, connecting to spectral methods via tilted generators and enabling reduction of multiscale systems. We survey computational approaches including minimum action methods, their geometric variants for quasipotential calculations, and neural network techniques. The Schlögl model of chemical bistability serves as a running example, illustrating both scalar and spatially extended settings. Appendices provide self-contained background on stochastic calculus and Markov jump processes.
Recent progress in the construction of Hadamard matrices
Ronan Egan; Ilias Kotsireas; Stephen London; Pádraig Ó Catháin

A Hadamard matrix is a square matrix with entries $\pm 1$ whose rows are mutually orthogonal. Hadamard matrices are conjectured to exist at every order divisible by $4$; for approximately the last twenty years, the smallest open case of this conjecture was order 668. In August 2026, Alpöge, Voinov and Reynolds-Haertle announced Hadamard matrices at the twelve orders below $2000$ at which none was known. In this paper we verify and analyse the claimed matrices. We survey results on the existence of Hadamard matrices and list the $95$ orders up to $10\,000$ at which no Hadamard matrix is currently known. In pursuing this work we constructed Hadamard matrices at sixteen orders that were open in the published literature. We conclude with a list of open problems.
Sionna Bench: Towards Benchmarks in Wireless Communications
Gian Marti; Jakob Hoydis; Fayçal Aït Aoudia; Sebastian Cammerer; Alexander Keller

Academic research in wireless communications has no tradition of benchmarks so far. Remarkable progress in benchmark-oriented fields like machine learning suggests that the adoption of benchmarks could benefit our field. In the absence of benchmarks, however, a scientific debt has accumulated: since the academic community has not canonized specific problem setups, methods that address essentially the same problem were often developed for slightly different setups and lack a common framework for comparison. Any attempt to establish a new benchmark is faced with the challenge of resolving this debt. Recent advances in agentic artificial intelligence (AI) create an opportunity to do so by leveraging AI-assisted coding. This makes it possible to implement the state-of-the art at scale and to adapt it to a common framework for comparison. We present Sionna Bench to initiate benchmarks in academic wireless communications research. As a pilot study, we use the problem of MIMO-OFDM channel estimation. At the time of writing, Sionna Bench's channel estimation benchmark features twenty channel estimation methods that were implemented from ten different papers. The ability to compare methods against the state-of-the-art will be crucial for navigating the research landscape in an era where AI-generated methods coexist with human-developed algorithms.
Structure-Preserving Numerical Schemes for a Time-Fractional Porous Medium Equation with Nonlocal Pressure

In this work, we study numerical approximations of the equation \begin{equation} \partial_t^αu-\nabla\cdot\left(u^{m-1}\nabla(-Δ)^{-σ}u\right)=0, \end{equation} where $0<α<1$, $0<σ<1$ and $m>1$. The Caputo derivative is discretized by the L1 formula, while the nonlinear nonlocal flux is approximated by a conservative upwind finite-difference scheme. We establish several structural properties of the implicit scheme in arbitrary space dimension, including a discrete maximum principle, non-negativity, mass conservation, $\ell^\infty$ and $\ell^2$ stability, existence of non-negative discrete solutions, and a discrete energy-dissipation estimate. Our assumptions include natural symmetry, a sign condition on the sum of the directional coefficients, and decay on the discrete weights. We also derive a consistency estimate for the complete nonlinear spatial operator. For rigorous convergence analysis, we restrict ourselves to one space dimension and introduce the cumulative variable associated with the density. This transforms the discrete problem into a monotone approximation of an equation involving the fractional Laplacian. Interestingly, for semigroup-based pressure-gradient weights, the resulting discrete operator is identified with the fractional discrete Laplacian. Next, using comparison and contraction properties of the integrated scheme, for $m\geq2$ and under the stated spatial regularity and weighted temporal consistency assumptions, we prove uniform convergence of the cumulative numerical solution and convergence of the corresponding density against compactly supported smooth test functions. The temporal estimates allow a weak singularity at the initial time. We also analyze an explicit variant of the scheme and derive a sufficient CFL condition covering the full range $0<σ<1$.
Quantum Fluctuations and Wigner Dynamics of a Carbon Nanotube Oscillator Driven by an Atomic Force Microscope

Suspended carbon nanotubes provide a useful platform for studying controlled nanomechanical motion in regimes where environmental fluctuations, memory effects, and quantum coherence can all influence the dynamics. We model the fundamental flexural mode of a carbon nanotube driven by an atomic force microscope as a harmonic quantum Brownian oscillator subject to a prescribed classical force and coupled linearly to a thermal environment. Starting from the generalized Langevin equation, we formulate the reduced dynamics directly in phase space, where the Wigner function evolves through a Gaussian propagator determined by dissipative linear transport, a deterministic force-induced displacement, and bath-induced fluctuations. For a Drude memory kernel, the retarded response is expressed through the three roots of a characteristic cubic equation. In the classical-noise limit, the three independent entries of the finite-time covariance matrix reduce to explicit finite sums over these response poles, eliminating numerical double-time covariance integration. We extend the construction to the full quantum fluctuation spectrum, obtaining a thermal frequency series representation that retains zero-point and low-temperature fluctuations. For an initial two-packet superposition, we examine interference attenuation and the integrated negative part of the Wigner function, which provides a phase space measure of nonclassicality. These results provide an explicit analytical framework for finite-memory quantum Brownian motion of bound oscillators and a tractable phase space description of driven carbon nanotube dynamics relevant to future quantum state preparation and quantum tomography experiments.
Central Limit Theorem for continuous $N$-particle systems in fixed- and high-temperature: single level

We characterize central limit theorems for polynomial linear statistics of continuous $N$-particle systems on $\mathbb R$, in both the fixed-temperature regime $θ=β/2>0$ and the high-temperature regime $Nθ\toγ>0$. In each regime, we give necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients of the logarithmic Bessel generating function, together with an explicit combinatorial formula for the limiting covariance. At fixed temperature, this formula recovers the classical second-order free moment--cumulant relation, up to the factor $1/θ$; at high temperature, it yields new second-order free $γ$-cumulants and their covariance relations. The proof combines moment extraction through Dunkl operators with a topological expansion of the logarithmic multivariate Bessel function indexed by ribbon graphs on surfaces. This expansion gives a topological interpretation of the free-cumulants: only genus zero contributes at fixed temperature, whereas arbitrarily high genera contribute at high temperature. As applications, we prove that $β$-addition preserves the CLT in both regimes and determine its limiting covariance from the input free cumulants, and establish a suitably rescaled transition from the high-temperature covariance to its fixed-temperature counterpart as $γ\to\infty$.
A periodic Anderson--Bernoulli model with infinitely many spectral gaps

We prove that the (almost-sure) spectrum of a periodic Anderson--Bernoulli model may enjoy infinitely many gaps. In particular, this shows that Schrödinger operators associated with transitive subshifts of finite type do not necessarily have finite-gap spectra. This resolves a pair of open problems posed by Damanik and the first named author. The main mechanism is the construction of a transverse heteroclinic connection within the class of Schrödinger transfer matrices, together with a scale-matching argument to produce a sequence of invariant multicones.
Exact spectral integrability of a finite-channel random Schrödinger operator: from fermionization of the Dyson--Riccati gas to Kontsevich integral
Yan V. Fyodorov; Pierre Le Doussal

We solve exactly, for arbitrary finite channel number $N$, the Riccati dynamics of a quasi-one-dimensional random matrix Schrödinger operator with Hermitian white-noise potential in the $β=2$ unitary symmetry class. The associated Dyson--Riccati eigenvalue gas admits an exact free-fermion representation at any sample length $L$, which in the limit $L\to \infty$ expresses the density of states and the total Lyapunov growth rate exactly through a single Airy Hankel $τ$-function providing multichannel generalization of $N=1$ Halperin--Thouless formulas. The $τ-$function further admits an outgoing-contour Kontsevich matrix Airy integral representation. Its saddle-point and double-scaling analyses give, in a unified way, the finite-channel density Lifshitz tail, and the large-$N$ spectral edge. In particular, for $N\gg 1$ the sharp $N=\infty$ edge is softened within an $N^{-4/5}$ spectral window, with its profile governed by the tritronquée solution of Painlevé I. We conjecture universality of this quasi-one-dimensional scaling edge profile for a broad class of $β=2$ random band matrices.
A Short Note on Algorithms For The Noisy $k$-XOR Problem

This mostly expository note studies the sample-noise regimes in which the testing problem for noisy $k$-XOR in dimension $n$ can be efficiently solved. Concretely, we ask what pairs $(β, δ)$ admit algorithms running in time $n^{O(k)}$ where $m = n^β, β\in [0,k]$ is the number of samples and $\mathsf{Bern}(n^{-δ}),δ\in (0,+\infty)$ is the noise distribution. The current state-of-the-art algorithms are: I. A folklore algorithm when $β> 1, δ>1$ based on Gaussian elimination; II. A folklore algorithm when $β\ge k/2$ based on the birthday paradox; III. A recent algorithm in the regime $β> δ+ k(1-δ), δ\in (0,1)$ based on a reduction to the first algorithm [DJ24,CSZ24]. IV. Extending [AF09], we strictly improve the last regime to $β> δ+ (k-1)(1-δ), δ\in (0,1).$ These algorithms correspond to efficiently finding short cycles in uniform hypergraphs and can be equivalently phrased as algorithmic Moore bounds.
Class polynomial obstructions to canonical congruences for the smallest parts function

We resolve an open conjecture by proving that the only "canonical'' Ramanujan congruence primes for the Andrews' smallest parts function, $\operatorname{spt}(n)$, are $\ell= 5, 7, 13$. Building on work of Ahlgren and Kim, we show that any such congruence forces square-index coefficients of certain weakly holomorphic forms of weight $1/2$ to vanish modulo the congruence prime. A normalized Borcherds product converts this into the vanishing of the derivative of a quotient of two oriented CM polynomials on $X_0(6)$. A quaternionic volume estimate in an Eichler order of level $6$ prevents that vanishing when a suitable inert discriminant is small. Treviño's character estimate supplies such a discriminant for every prime at least $10^{11}$. The remaining range is covered by the previous calculations of Ahlgren and Kim. These results have been verified in Lean by AxiomProver.
BIBO stability in infinite dimensions: extensions and limitations of finite-dimensional theory

The study of bounded-input bounded-output (BIBO) stability of infinite-dimensional systems gives rise to difficulties that do not occur in the classical finite-dimensional setting. In this paper, we resolve several questions concerning the definition and characterisation of BIBO stability in the framework of system nodes. In particular, we show that $\mathrm C^\infty$-BIBO stability need not imply $L^\infty$-BIBO stability in general, but that the two notions are equivalent when the output space is reflexive. Furthermore, we investigate to what extent classical results extend to the infinite-dimensional setting, including the relation between BIBO stability and exponential stability under controllability and observability assumptions.
Counterexamples to a conjecture and improved bounds for bipanchromatic colorings

We study the bipanchromatic number $χ_B$, introduced by Lalou et al. (Discrete Appl. Math. 391 (2026), 511-522) as the maximum number of colors in a panchromatic hypergraph coloring where every color appears at least twice. They show that merging uniquely occurring colors in a maximum panchromatic coloring gives the lower bound $β=χ_P-\lceilα/2\rceil \leq χ_B$, where $χ_P$ is the panchromatic number and $α$ is the minimum number of such colors among maximum panchromatic colorings. They conjectured that $χ_B=β$ and subsequently disproved it (arXiv:2610.08042). We identify the smallest counterexample, with six vertices and three hyperedges, both minimum possible. We show that the ratio bound $χ_B/β<2$ is asymptotically sharp and prove minimality results for the order and hyperedge count. For $3\leα<χ_P$ we show that every integer from $β$ to $χ_P-1$ occurs as $χ_B$ while $χ_P$ and $α$ are held fixed. Furthermore, we discover that the values $|V|,χ_P,α$ directly decide whether the conjectured equality holds except when $α=4$, where a matching reduction resolves the ambiguity. We derive the optimal universal lower bound $L$ depending only on $|V|,χ_P,α$ in the nontrivial regime $0<2α<|V|$. Finally, we prove $χ_B/L\le5/4$ and $χ_B/L\le6/5+1/(5L)$, with $5/4$ sharp and $6/5$ asymptotically sharp as $L\to\infty$.
Supercritical Branching Random Walks on Nested Lattices

In classical models of supercritical continuous-time branching random walks (BRWs) on a $d$-dimensional lattice, the dimension $d$ is typically assumed to be fixed. When comparing the exponential growth rate $λ_0$ of a particle population in a BRW with a single branching source across lattices of different dimensions, a question arises whether it is possible to construct a family of random walks on $d$-dimensional lattices such that the model for a $(d+1)$-dimensional lattice ``inherits'' the properties of the model for a $d$-dimensional lattice in a meaningful sense. To address this question, the paper introduces the concept of a ``random walk on nested lattices'' and investigates the effect of the dimension $d$ on particle population growth using the ``inheritance'' condition. For an arbitrary symmetric random walk, a limit theorem is proved on the representation of the positive eigenvalue of the evolution operator for the mean particle numbers in terms of the process parameters and the dimension $d$, as the branching source intensity $β\to \infty$. The theorem shows that the influence of dimension persists even for very strong branching.
Normal approximation for subgraph counts in random intersection graphs: the case of cliques

Let $X^{(r)}_n$ denote the number of copies of a complete graph $K_r$ in the random intersection graph model on $n$ vertices. We derive upper bounds on the distance between the standardized version of $X^{(r)}_n$ and the standard normal distribution, measured in both the Kolmogorov and Wasserstein metrics. We complement these results with necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic normality. As a byproduct, we provide precise estimates for the variance of $X^{(r)}_n$. In the process, we develop new general techniques for analysing so--called clique covers, which play a crucial role in the study of subgraph probabilities in random intersection graphs.
Short Point Lists for CNFs and Stronger Constant-Depth Circuit Hardness

We give a short-description decomposition of bounded-width CNFs. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, every width-$b$ CNF on $m$ variables is an exact disjoint union of at most $2^{\varepsilon m}$ width-$b$ CNFs, each determined by $2^{O_\varepsilon(b)}\log(m+1)$ satisfying assignments. For every fixed $d\ge3$, we prove a worst-case size lower bound of $2^{Ω_d((n\log n)^{1/(d-1)})}$ against depth-at-most-$d$ unbounded-fan-in AND/OR circuits with input negations for three polynomial-time Boolean families: inverse trace over binary fields, the Goldreich--Tal trilinear function, and OpenAI's polynomial evaluator with its original parameters. All parameter bits count as inputs. For inverse trace, every such circuit of size at most $S$, where $n\le S\le2^{c_dn^{1/(d-1)}}$, has uniform sign correlation at most $2^{-η_dn\log\log S/(\log S)^{d-1}}$. Here $c_d,η_d>0$ depend only on $d$. This improves on the classical parity correlation bound. The lower bounds combine the decomposition with restriction arguments; the correlation bound additionally uses common partial decision trees. We also construct exact nonuniform AND/OR circuits for inverse trace of size $2^{O(n^{2/3})}$ at depth eight and $2^{O(\sqrt n\log n)}$ at depth nine. For every fixed integer $h\ge2$, the construction gives depth-$(4h+1)$ circuits of size $2^{O_h(n^{1/h}\log n)}$. The upper bounds implement finite-field evaluation and interpolation using circuits that enumerate intermediate states.
Orthogonal group sections via light bulb systems

For any oriented, smooth $4$--manifold $X$ diffeomorphic to $(S^2\times S^2)^{\# n}\# D^4$, this paper shows that the natural group homomorphism $$\mathrm{Mod}(X,\partial X)\to \mathrm{O}(H_2(X;\mathbb{Z}))$$ admits a section. In fact, every light bulb system in $X$ gives rise to a section, which can be characterized uniquely in terms of implanted barbell twists and implanted crossbell involutions. Moreover, all sections arising from different light bulb systems become identical after a single $S^2\times S^2$--stabilization of $X$.
A note on the hypercomplex singular Cauchy-like integral in Douglis analysis
Isidro Paulino-Basurto; Jean Marie Vilaire; José Oscar González-Cervantes; Juan Bory-Reyes

Hypercomplex analysis extends classical complex analysis to Douglis algebras, replacing holomorphic functions with hyperanalytic functions, i.e., null solutions of the Douglis operator in $\mathbb R^2$ (identifying $\mathbb R^2$ with $\mathbb C$). The hypercomplex singular Cauchy-like integral, is one of the main actors in the hypercomplex analysis and many properties have been studied in recently decades. This paper aims to present local estimates of the hypercomplex singular Cauchy-like integral.
Subgraph probabilities in random intersection graphs

Since their introduction by Karoński, Scheinerman, and Singer-Cohen in 90's, random intersection graphs have attracted much attention, mostly due to their various applications. In this article, we establish a general result for the probability that a given small subgraph is present in a random intersection graph. Our theorem applies to a broad range of parameters, including regimes that have not previously been considered in the literature. Moreover, it extends known results and situates them within a broader framework, making this approach a convenient tool for comparing the probabilities of graphs in the random intersection graph model. To prove our main result, we develop new proof techniques that, to the best of our knowledge, have not previously been employed in the study of small subgraphs in random intersection graphs. Many special cases and examples are presented as well.
Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
Cheng Peng; Xuao Zhang; Ziruo Zhang

The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of integer partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. The free energy of the interpolating solutions cannot be matched with the on-shell action of any known bulk solution. The $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies can be computed analytically. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.
Tree Lattices and the Neumann-Zagier conjecture
Joshua Evan Greene; Ahmad Issa; Duncan McCoy

A tree with integer weights on its vertices presents an integral lattice called a tree lattice. We prove that if a tree lattice is positive definite, then one of the vertex elements is irreducible, i.e. determines a facet of its Voronoi polyhedron. As a corollary, we settle a 1985 conjecture of Neumann and Zagier: if a tree lattice is isometric to the lattice of integer points in Euclidean space, then the tree contains a vertex of weight one.
We show that the problem of deciding whether a simplicial complex is partitionable is NP-complete in dimensions two and higher, answering a 1995 question of Kleinschmidt and Onn.
Flux Vacua, Asymptotic Periods, and Relatively Anosov Representations

We develop a topological method to detect classical flux vacua of M-theory on Calabi-Yau fourfolds with a single complex structure modulus using only asymptotic period data and monodromy information. To this end, we express the index of the F-term of the flux superpotential as a winding number along the boundary of the universal cover of the complex structure moduli space. The index evaluates to a sum over zeros and poles of a suitably normalized boundary F-term, where local contributions can be computed algebraically on a dense set of boundary points. Assuming a conjectured bound on the remaining contributions, sufficiently many sign changes of the boundary F-term guarantee a flux vacuum in the interior. We illustrate the method on the mirror Fermat sextic with explicit examples and a systematic flux scan. A main technical ingredient in our construction is a continuity result for projective period maps: we prove that the non-holomorphic (3,1)-period map extends continuously to the boundary of the covering space if the monodromy representation is relatively Anosov. In general, this property does not hold for holomorphic (4,0)-periods.
Boundary One-Point Functions in the Open XXZ Spin Chain with Generic Integrable Boundaries
Till Bargheer; Tengis Batmunkh; Paul Ryan

We consider the problem of computing observables beyond the spectrum in the open XXZ spin chain with the most generic integrable boundary conditions. For such boundaries, the residual u(1) symmetry is broken and the familiar Baxter TQ equation describing the spectrum becomes inhomogeneous, placing the model outside the realm of existing approaches to correlation functions and form factors. We show that the Functional Separation of Variables method, so far developed mainly for rational, (quasi-)periodic spin chains, is largely insensitive to these modifications, and works equally well for diagonal and generic boundaries. Using this method, we compute exact determinant expressions for a prototypical example of form factors in open-boundary systems, namely the longitudinal and transverse boundary-spin one-point functions in arbitrary Hamiltonian eigenstates at finite system size. No constraint relating the two boundary configurations and no reference state are required. We verify the resulting formulae against direct finite-volume diagonalisation.
Hypercomplex Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs

A hypercomplex method for constructing solutions of a class of nonlinear partial differential equations is developed. A family of two-dimensional commutative associative algebras is introduced in which the structural coefficients depend on a component of the monogenic function itself. A corresponding theory of monogenic functions is developed, and nonlinear analogues of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions are obtained. It is shown that the first component of a monogenic function satisfies a broad class of second-order nonlinear partial differential equations whose coefficients depend on the unknown function. A hodograph transformation is used to linearize the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system. As a result, the problem of constructing solutions of the nonlinear equations is reduced to solving a second-order linear partial differential equation with variable coefficients, followed by the inverse hodograph transformation. A local correspondence between solutions of the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system and solutions of the associated linear equation is established, yielding a constructive algorithm for generating solutions of the original nonlinear PDEs. Several examples are presented in which explicit and implicit solutions of nonlinear second-order PDEs are obtained by this method.
On Diophantine tuples involving star numbers

In this paper, we discuss two related Diophantine tuple problems involving star numbers $S_n=6n(n-1)+1$. First, we investigate classical $D(k)$-tuples whose elements are star numbers. We construct infinitely many $D(k)$-pairs for several positive and negative admissible values of $k$, and we prove several nonexistence results for $D(k)$-triples and quadruples. Second, we introduce a modified notion of a star number $D(k)$-tuple, requiring $a_ia_j+k$ itself to be a star number. We construct several infinite families of $D(1)$-triples, and study their extensions to quadruples. In particular, we prove that $\{4,108,165\}$ has the unique extension $\{4,108,165,360\}$ to a star number $D(1)$-quadruple. The main tools used in this paper are generalized Pell equations, Nagell's theorem, lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms due to Matveev and Dujella-Pethő version of the Baker-Davenport reduction method in diophantine approximation.
Approximability of Triangulated Categories under Separable Extensions
Mengzhen Zhu; Yuefei Zheng; Xianhui Fu

In this paper, we investigate the behavior of approximability under separable extensions of triangulated categories.
