Maximum rank-distance codes were introduced independently by Delsarte (1978) and Gabidulin (1985) for unrestricted matrix spaces, and their study was subsequently extended to the classical form spaces of alternating, symmetric, and Hermitian matrices. For Hermitian $d$-codes, Schmidt (2018) established the upper bound and constructed optimal additive codes for all admissible parameters except when $n$ and $d$ are both even and $4\le d\le n-2$. We settle this final open existence case, more generally, construct additive maximum Hermitian rank-metric codes for every admissible length and minimum distance. Rather than working directly in the space of Hermitian matrices, we construct our objects within central simple algebras with unitary involution arising from quotients of skew polynomial rings. We also introduce scalar-field and Lyapunov operators in these algebras, leading to new invariants for the equivalence of additive Hermitian codes. Explicitly determining these invariants yields strong necessary conditions for Hermitian equivalence and demonstrates that our construction contains a large number of pairwise inequivalent codes.
Compactness and weak compactness of linearized Holomorphic-Lipschitz maps
Frédéric Bayart; Mathis Lemay; Colin Petitjean

Any holomorphic Lipschitz map $f$, defined on the open unit ball $B_X$ of a complex Banach space $X$ and taking values in a complex Banach space $Y$, can be uniquely and canonically associated with a bounded linear operator $\widehat f : \mathcal G_0(B_X) \longrightarrow \mathcal G_0(Y)$ between the corresponding holomorphic Lipschitz-free spaces. The aim of this paper is to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the compactness and weak compactness of such operators. In particular, we obtain a general characterisation of the compactness of $\widehat f$ in terms of metric properties of its symbol $f$. We then focus on the case where the target space is a subspace of $\ell_p$, $1\leq p<\infty$. When the target space is $\ell_1$, we show that compactness and weak compactness of $\widehat f$ are both equivalent to $\widehat f$ not fixing a copy of $\ell_1$. Finally, when the target space is $\ell_p$ with $1<p<\infty$, we obtain a metric characterisation of the weak compactness of $\widehat f$. As a consequence, we show that compactness and weak compactness need not coincide, even when the target space is $\ell_p$.
Lagrangian invariant tori for completely resonant nonlinear Schr{ö}dinger equations

We study small solutions of the parameterless nonlinear Schr{ö}dinger equations on the circle. In this regime, the nonlinearity is perturbative and the system is thus nearly integrable. We prove the persistence, in the presence of nonlinearity, of full-dimensional tori. We justify this denomination by proving that they are Lagrangian in the sense that, although they are not submanifolds (since they are compact), at every point their tangent cone is a Lagrangian subspace. This is the first result of this type for an equation without an infinity of external random parameters. We achieve this by establishing new fine decay and uniformity properties of the amplitude-to-frequency map. This is the main technical novelty of this paper. It allows us to modulate all the frequencies and thus obtain non-resonance conditions without any assumption on the choice of the tangential sites.
Dual Reflection Groups from Solutions to the Yang--Baxter Equation

Suppose that $r: X^2 \to X^2$ is a nondegenerate, involutive solution to the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation. To this data, we can associate an Artin--Schelter regular algebra $A$ and an infinite family of groups $G_k$, where $k \geqslant 1$. For each $k$, we show that $G_k$ is a dual reflection group for $A$, in the sense the component of $A$ graded by $1_{G_k}$ is again Artin--Schelter regular. We also show that, using the additional structure afforded by the underlying solution to the Yang--Baxter equation, one can determine the centre, Koszul complex, and associated twisted superpotential for $A$.
Sharp thresholds and convergence for a nonlocal bistable equation

We study $u_t=J*u-u+f(u)$ on $\R^d$ with a bistable reaction and radial nonincreasing probability kernels. Under the stated hypotheses, every solution from compactly supported data between zero and one converges to zero, locally to one, or to a single nonzero decaying stationary state. At every nonzero decaying stationary state between zero and one, we assume either nondegeneracy up to translations or analyticity of the reaction near the closure of the state's range. Decaying limits are strictly radially decreasing, with centers in the initial support's closed convex hull. For $u_0=\mathbf1_{B_R}$, we give explicit threshold bounds; analyticity near $[0,1]$ yields a unique critical radius with a nonzero stationary limit.
Half-sized gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function

Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we prove that the lower limit of the normalised gaps between consecutive zeros of the Riemann zeta function is at most $1/2$. Our methods utilise a more efficient method for detecting gaps with short Dirichlet polynomials. Specifically, we apply resonance to a quotient of shifted zeta functions, rather than to the number of zeros in a short interval, using a Möbius resonator adapted to the symmetry between the shifts.
MONODROMY AND BIG QUANTUM COHOMOLOGY OF HYPERPLANE SECTIONS OF (CO)ADJOINT VARIETIES
Vladimiro Benedetti; Simone Billi; Nicolas Perrin

We study the monodromy representation of general hyperplane sections of (co)adjoint varieties. We apply this result to reduce the generic semisemplicity of the big quantum cohomology to its ambient part, and to prove that the big quantum cohomology of general hyperplane sections of IGr(2, 6) is generically semisimple and satisfies Dubrovin's conjecture.
Twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes and the rational hit conjecture

We study the top degree concentration property for the cohomology of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes of multiarrangements of hyperplanes. Our main tool is a short exact sequence of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes based on the deletion-restriction exact sequences for logarithmic differential forms found recently by Abe and Denham. We prove a number of general results that can be used to establish the top degree cohomology concentration property, and also establish that property for some families of multiarrangements. As a consequence of our results, we prove the rational hit conjecture of R.~M.~W.~Wood about the coinvariants of the rational Steenrod algebra acting on the polynomial ring. We also make progress on the deformed version of that conjecture proposed by Hivert and Thiéry, prove generalizations of the rational hit conjecture for all complex reflection groups $G(m,p,n)$, thus answering questions of Bergeron, Borie and Thiéry, and generalize the rational hit conjecture to all standard subalgebras of the rational Steenrod algebra.
On the Adaptive Covering Complexity of Strings: Unifying Relative and Self-Referential Compression

We introduce and study the adaptive covering complexity C adapt S (s), defined as the minimum number of contiguous factor blocks required to partition a string s when each block is either a factor of a fixed external dictionary S or a factor of the target's already decoded prefix. This hybrid admissibility model formalizes the structural interaction between static dictionary matching and dynamic nonoverlapping self-referencing. Our main theoretical result is the exact logarithmic law which is tight and proves that dynamic self-reference can reduce phrase count by at most an exponential factor over static dictionary covering alone. We establish structural equivalences showing that the measure bridges word-segmented Relative Lempel-Ziv and non-overlapping LZ77, and we prove exact preset-history LZ77 sandwich bounds. Furthermore, we establish the optimality of the longest-match greedy parse via an exchange lemma and present an optimal implementation based on dual suffix automata running in O(M + n) time and space for a constant alphabet. These analytical results are complemented by counting bounds, stationary-ergodic asymptotic invariance, a dictionaryselection NP-hardness result, and a concise empirical illustration.
Max Fathi; Arnaud Guillin; Cyril Labbé; Justin Salez

We study how a relaxed gradient estimate is enough to prove cutoff for several new families of Markov processes, within the varentropy framework of [Sal25]. In particular, we show how certain regularization estimates from hypocoercivity theory allow one to prove cutoff for kinetic dynamics. Moreover, we prove cutoff for some families of diffusions with non-convex potentials and for mean-field dynamics, as well as for biased random walks on the symmetric group, giving a simple proof of a far-reaching extension of a result of [NY24].
Bernoulli property for skew products of exponentially mixing systems over Anosov bases

We study $C^{1+β}$ skew products over topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphisms, with fiber dynamics generated by a locally free $\mathbb{R}^k$-action. For a Gibbs measure on the base and a cocycle with a nonzero average, we establish a Bernoulli criterion for ergodic invariant product measures. The fiber hypotheses apply to actions that are exponentially mixing with respect to the SRB measure, as well as volume measures that are almost exponentially mixing with a limit SRB measure. As an application, when the fibers are generated by geodesic flows or Weyl chamber actions, our results reveal a statistical phase transition determined by the drift.
Quadratic growth rigidity for the complex Monge--Ampère equation
For the complex Monge--Ampère equation on $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, we prove the Liouville theorem for solutions with quadratic growth.
Herzog Class of Codimension $3$ Licci Monomial Ideals

Let $S$ be the polynomial ring in three variables with homogeneous maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$. Licci ideals are ideals that can be linked by a finite number of steps to a complete intersection. All licci ideals admit a rigid deformation, and two licci ideals are said to be in the same Herzog class if they have a common rigid deformation. Guerrieri-Ni-Weyman gave a parametrization for the Herzog classes of codimension $3$ licci ideals in terms of pairs of partitions associated to Schur functors. In this paper, we give an explicit formula that determines the Herzog class of a given $\mathfrak{m}$-primary licci monomial ideal.
A note on the solution to the standard normal Stein equation

For $z\in\mathbb{R}$ we reconsider the solution $f_z$ to the standard normal Stein equation, corresponding to the Kolmogorov distance for distributions on the real line. More precisely, we prove the Lipschitz continuity of the related function $x\mapsto ρ_z(x):=xf_z(x)$ and explain how this observation may help to remove some unnecessary technical conditions from recent Berry-Esseen bounds in the literature around the Malliavin-Stein method. We further show that the Lipschitz constants of the functions $ρ_z$ are yet not uniformly bounded in $z$ and discuss consequences of this negative result.
On the simultaneous zeroes of Bessel processes

Given n independent squared Bessel processes, a priori with different dimensions, we investigate the first time $ζ$ at which at least n -1 of them vanish simultaneously. We show that the tail asymptotics of $ζ$ admits a power decay, with a persistence exponent given as the first positive pole of some explicit meromorphic function. This answers a question raised by Q. Berger, L. B{é}thencourt and C. Tardif in the case n = 3. We also provide along the way a closed-form expression for the Mellin transform of the position of the remaining process at time $ζ$. The paper is concluded by a more detailed study of the case of identical dimensions.
Complex Analytic Structure of Hybrid Classes of Generalized Polynomial-like Mappings
Miaokeyan Lin; Weixiao Shen; Yimin Wang

In this paper, we study hybrid classes of generalized polynomial-like mappings. We show that locally they are complex analytic submanifolds with finite codimension equal to the total order of critical points in the filled Julia set (counting multiplicity).
When vector abundance constrains vector-borne transmission: inside epidemic dynamics within a prescribed population
Lise Isnel; Julien Papa{ï}x; Olivier Bonnefon; Samuel Soubeyrand; Lionel Roques

The global burden of vector-borne diseases continues to rise, presenting escalating challenges to public health and agricultural systems. Their expanding geographic range and associated impacts underscore the need for tools to project disease dynamics and evaluate interventions. Mechanistic compartmental host--vector models provide such a framework by explicitly representing transmission processes. However, while these models often couple vector population dynamics with infection spread, the inherent complexity of vector demographic processes calls for a more modular approach. In this study, we consider the setting in which the total vector abundance is an externally-prescribed input to a general vector-mediated transmission model. Our objectives are threefold: (i) to provide theoretical guarantees for ensuring consistency between the prescribed total vector abundance and the dynamics of the model compartments, (ii) to characterize model properties related to the local reproduction index (informing extinction or emergence near the time of introduction) and the inter-seasonal propagation, and (iii) to derive insights for diseases transmitted by Aedes albopictus in mainland France. We apply this framework by feeding the epidemiological model with vector-abundance data obtained either from entomological surveillance systems or from an external detailed population dynamic model. Moreover, epidemiological national surveillance data are used to estimate the transmission parameter. Based on this, we derive conditions for emergence and extinction, and show how the extent of the epidemic depends on introduction timing, transmission rate, and susceptible population density. Taken together, these results highlight the value of generating and leveraging entomological surveillance data as well as their model-based counterparts when observations are unavailable (which is particularly relevant in the context of global warming and for the evaluation of vector-control strategies). Overall, we establish a refined framework integrating such data or forecast into compartmental models, with strong potential for a wide range of applications in animal, human or plant health.
Size Ramsey numbers of star forests with two components on one side

We determine the size Ramsey number of a two-component star forest versus an arbitrary star forest. Let $q,a,b,n_1,\ldots,n_q$ be positive integers with $a\ge b$ and $n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_q$. We prove that \[ \begin{split} \rhat\left(K_{1,a}\sq K_{1,b}, \bigsqcup_{i=1}^{q}K_{1,n_i}\right) ={}&(a+n_1-1) +\sum_{i=1}^{q-1}\max\{a+n_{i+1}-1,b+n_i-1\}\\ &+(b+n_q-1). \end{split} \] This proves the conjecture of Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp (Erdős Problem~\#561) in the case where one of the two star forests has exactly two components. The formula holds without any restriction on the parity of the star sizes. The proof combines vertex deletion, iterated matching deletion, and Lovász's factor theorem.

We use spectral methods to determine Turán coefficients of signed graphs under containment that preserves negative edges and allows positive edges to be realized by either sign. For a fixed forbidden signed graph $\sF$ with at least one edge, the coefficient $\tht(\sF)$ is the supremum of the weights $ρ\ge1$ for which every $\sF$-free signed graph $\sG$ of order $n$ satisfies $e^+(\sG)+ρe^-(\sG)\le\binom n2+o(n^2)$. We prove a variational characterization of the weighted extremal density and show that $\tht(\sF)=1+1/L(\sF)$, where $L(\sF)$ is the supremum of the adjacency spectral radii of $\sF$-admissible graphs. The coefficient is infinite exactly when the underlying graph $F$ is bipartite, and equals one exactly when $F$ has no independent set meeting every negative edge. When $χ(F)=3$, the possible coefficients are exactly $1$, $3/2$, $1+1/\sqrt3$, $(1+\sqrt5)/2$, $1+1/\sqrt2$, and $2$, each of which is realized by a signed graph. In this case, if $\tht(\sF)>1$, then $L(\sF)$ is attained by an admissible graph on at most five vertices, and the order bound is sharp. More generally, when some path is inadmissible, we obtain explicit order bounds for connected admissible graphs with bounded maximum degree. We also derive restrictions on the algebraic degree and rational values of $\tht(\sF)$.
On the Information Bottleneck for Ergodic Finite-State Markov Chains: Stationary Approximation and Asymptotic Optimality
Wael Tabbara; Jihad Fahs; Mohamad Assaad

In this paper, we investigate the information bottleneck problem for sources that follow discrete-time ergodic finite-state Markov chains. We propose treating observations generated by the time-varying Markov chain as if they were drawn from its unique stationary distribution, and we use the solution to the information bottleneck problem for the stationary process to compress samples from the time-varying process. The resulting error is upper bounded by several information gap terms. We establish sufficient conditions under which these gaps converge to zero and analyze the convergence rates of the different information gap terms. The proofs are based on intricate analysis using convergence of subsequences along with the derivation of properties of the optimization sets associated with the information bottleneck problem. In addition to the inequalities and convergence results we establish, our analysis offers insights into how simple properties of ergodic Markov chains give rise to results concerning the information bottleneck problem for such chains.
The existence of symmetric cyclic Steiner quadruple systems

A Steiner quadruple system of order $v$, denoted by $\operatorname{SQS}(v)$, is called cyclic if it admits $\mathbb Z_v$ as a group of automorphisms acting regularly on its point set. A cyclic system is called symmetric cyclic, or S-cyclic, if the multiplier $-1$ preserves each block orbit individually. Grannell and Griggs conjectured in 1983 that such a system of order $v$ exists if and only if $v\equiv2,4,10,20\pmod{24}$ and every odd prime divisor $p$ of $v$ satisfies $p\equiv1$ or $5\pmod{12}$. This paper proves the conjecture. The main step is to construct an $S$-cyclic Steiner quadruple system of order $2p$ for every prime $p\equiv1\pmod4$. Together with existing reduction theorems, these constructions determine which finite abelian groups admit a symmetric group-invariant Steiner quadruple system.
The asymptotic stability of the stable solitons of the generalized good Boussinesq equation
Junsik Bae; Scipio Cuccagna; Daniele Del Santo; Masaya Maeda

This paper continues the series where we apply a synthesis of the virial inequalities in the tradition of Merle, Martel and their collaborators and of Kato smoothing, to close the virial inequalities. We prove absence of nonzero imaginary eigenvalues for the linearization in unweighted space and asymptotic stability for every velocity $\frac{\sqrt{p-1}}{2}<c<1$ and every $1<p<5$.
Single-level reformulations for network pricing under Wardrop equilibrium with separable affine costs

We consider the problem of setting tolls on a subset of the arcs of a congested network so as to maximize the revenue of a network authority, anticipating that users route according to a Wardrop equilibrium. This problem is naturally cast as a bilevel program in which the leader sets tolls while the followers respond by choosing an equilibrium routing. We focus on the important special case of separable affine arc cost functions. Under this assumption, Wardrop equilibria admit Beckmann's convex characterization, from which we derive three new single-level reformulations of the bilevel problem, exploiting both Beckmann's formulation and its dual: an arc-based formulation, which we solve exactly, and two path-based formulations, solved by column-and-constraint generation. Beyond the reformulations, we further derive from Beckmann's potential an upper bound on the optimal revenue that can be used to certify optimality gaps across all formulations. An extensive computational study on instances derived from the Sioux Falls and Eastern Massachusetts networks compares our formulations with the recent mixed-integer nonlinear formulation of Beck, Labbé and Schmidt. The arc-based formulation solves substantially more instances to proven optimality (within a time limit of 1800 s) than this formulation and, unlike it, returns a feasible solution on every instance. It remains effective on the largest, 74-node network, on which the formulation of Beck et al. solves none. The magnitude of the upper bounds on the tolls proves to be a major driver of tractability: the genuinely hard core of the benchmark emerges once the regulatory cap on tolls is removed. The two path-based formulations, used as heuristics, return a solution within one percent of the optimum on every instance whose optimal value is known, often in seconds where exact formulations reach the time limit.
Structural Identifiability in Non-Gaussian Graphical Discrete Lyapunov Models

This paper studies the problem of structural identifiability for graphical discrete Lyapunov models in the non-Gaussian setting from observational data. A graphical discrete Lyapunov model associated with a graph $G$ consists of the set of stationary distributions of stable first-order vector autoregressive models whose transition matrices have sparsity patterns determined by $G$. This model has a causal interpretation as $G$ can be viewed as encoding dynamic causal relationships between random variables of interest. It has been shown that generic parameter identifiability holds for reflexive directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). Structural identifiability for these models remains unstudied beyond certain restrictive cases. In this work, we prove a non-constructive structural identifiability result for reflexive DAGs in non-Gaussian graphical discrete Lyapunov models by leveraging the information contained in the entire collection of stationary cumulants. We also provide a concrete algorithm for learning reflexive directed trees from stationary cumulants of orders $\leq 5$.
Gaussian equivalence for CNN with non-Gaussian weights

We study the infinite-width limit of convolutional neural networks with random weights and show that the Gaussian process limit does not require Gaussian priors. Assuming that the weights are i.i.d., centered, and have sufficiently many finite moments, converges weakly in the space of continuous functions on the compact input set to independent copies of a centered Gaussian process. Our framework accommodates activation functions of polynomial growth together with a broad class of patch-extraction operators, covering standard convolutions, padding, stride, and common pooling mechanisms.
Jonathan Brundan; Alistair Savage; Ben Webster

We show that locally finite Abelian module categories over the affine Brauer category are the same thing as locally finite Abelian 2-representations of a certain 2-iquantum group satisfying some additional nilpotency and finiteness properties. Our results are valid over algebraically closed fields of characteristic other than 2 and for arbitrary spectra. This extends recent work of Gao, Rui and Song, who treated characteristic 0 with half-integral spectrum. The relevant Satake diagrams are of quasi-split type AIII and of diagonal type A, including affine types in positive characteristic. The key step in our approach identifies the affine Brauer category with a topologically dense monoidal subcategory of a completion of the 2-iquantum group. As an application, we show that deformed cyclotomic quotients on the two sides are equivalent.
A fast Laguerre--Fourier spectral method for the polyatomic Boltzmann collision operator with continuous internal energ
Pei Zhang; Yanli Wang; Zhenning Cai

The polyatomic Boltzmann equation extends the classical kinetic description to gases whose molecules possess internal energy in addition to their translational motion. The distribution function then has one more variable than in the monatomic case, and the collision operator becomes an eight-fold integral whose evaluation dominates the cost of solving the equation. In this work, we propose a fast Laguerre--Fourier spectral method for the polyatomic Boltzmann equation with continuous internal energy, which evaluates the collision operator in $O(K^2MN^4\log N + K^3MN^4)$ online operations after a solution-independent precomputation, where $N$ is the number of Fourier modes in each velocity direction, $K$ is the number of Laguerre modes and $M$ is the number of quadrature points on the sphere. Specifically, the distribution function is expanded in generalized Laguerre functions in the internal energy and in Fourier modes in velocity. A sequence of changes of variables then separates the internal-energy integrals from the velocity convolutions, so that the former no longer involve the distribution function and are computed once and stored. Numerical experiments are presented for both the spatially homogeneous and the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation. They confirm the spectral accuracy of the proposed method and its agreement with the direct simulation Monte Carlo method.
Approximation numbers of critical Besov embeddings

We determine the approximation numbers of critical embeddings between isotropic Besov spaces on nonempty bounded Lipschitz domains in any dimension. For 0 < p_1 < 2 < p_2 <= infinity and s_1 - s_2 = d max{1/p_1, 1 - 1/p_2} > d(1/p_1 - 1/p_2), the approximation numbers have order N^{-1/2}(log(e+N))^Gamma for every 0 < q_1, q_2 <= infinity, with an explicit four-case formula for Gamma. This resolves the strictly compact critical Besov approximation-number problem identified in Vybiral's overview. For q_1 < q_2, the logarithmic exponent depends on the ordering of p_1' and p_2; it can vanish for one pair (p_1,p_2) and remain positive for another with the same fine indices. A row estimate for the approximation error gives lower bounds when the target fine index is below one. Gaussian finite-rank approximations acting on several levels give the sharp upper bounds when Gamma < 1/2. For q_1 < q_2, matching lower bounds for the two strict orderings of the inner indices follow from Malykhin's finite-window estimates and norm comparisons. The results include quasi-Banach indices and the full spaces of bounded coefficient sequences at infinite fine indices.

We present a proof for the $(n-2)$-linear extension estimate for curved surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge5$, at the local product exponent $2(n-1)/(n-2)^2$, with an arbitrarily small power loss. The hypotheses are transversality of the normals and nondegeneracy of the compressed shape operators on their common two-dimensional orthogonal complement. The argument combines polynomial partitioning, a descent through algebraic varieties, localized multilinear restriction, and positive packet-energy estimates.
Invitation to torso parameters of annotated graphs
Maël Dumas; Jędrzej Hodor; Tomasz Mazur; Piotr Micek; Clément Rambaud; Giannos Stamoulis

An annotated graph is a pair $(G,S)$, where $G$ is a graph and $S$ is a subset of vertices of $G$. We present a unified approach for definitions of annotated versions of classical graph parameters such as treewidth, pathwidth, treedepth, etc. A generic way to incorporate a distinguished set of vertices into a graph parameter is via torsos. Given a graph $G$ and a subset $S'\subseteq V(G)$, we define $\mathrm{torso}_G(S')$ to be the graph with vertex set $S'$ in which distinct vertices $u,v\in S'$ are adjacent if and only if there exists a $u$-$v$ path in $G$ whose internal vertices lie outside $S'$. Now let $\mathrm{p}$ be any graph parameter. For an annotated graph $(G,S)$, we define the torso $\mathrm{p}$ of $(G,S)$ by \[\mathrm{p}(G,S) = \min\{\mathrm{p}(\mathrm{torso}_G(S')) \mid S \subset S' \subset V(G)\}.\] For a minor-closed class of annotated graphs $\mathcal{C}$, we discuss equivalent conditions for $\mathrm{p}(G,S)$ bounded for all $(G,S)\in\mathcal{C}$ in terms of annotated graphs excluded in $\mathcal{C}$. In many cases, we collect known results from the literature. We include two new arguments for $\mathrm{p}$ being the $2$-treedepth and the feedback vertex number. Among other statements, we also include a variant of the Erdős-Pósa property for annotated cycles. We propose some new research directions.
On nilpotent Lie algebras arising from parabolic subalgebras and quivers --- three-step cases

Nilpotent Lie groups are important subjects for studying spacial left-invariant geometric structures. However, nilpotent Lie groups are impossible to classify, and even the two-step case has not been classified. There are several classes of examples of nilpotent Lie algebras that arise with higher nilpotency steps. In this paper, we focus on two of these methods. The first one is the nilpotent parts of parabolic subalgebras of semisimple Lie algebras. The second one is the nilpotent Lie algebras obtained by quivers. We list and compare nilpotent Lie algebras obtained by these two methods that are three-step and of dimension at most 10.
Exact extremizers for $\ell_p$-judicious bisections of triangle-free graphs

Balogh, Clemen and Lidický asked how large the minimum $\ell_p$-norm of the internal-edge counts over balanced partitions of an $n$-vertex triangle-free graph can be. For each fixed $2<p<\infty$ and all sufficiently large even $n$, we determine this value exactly for bisections and characterize all extremal graphs. They are precisely the complete bipartite graphs $K_{a,n-a}$ for which $a\le n/2$ maximizes an explicit integer objective. All maximizing values of $a$ lie in an interval of length bounded in terms of $p$ alone. We also prove quantitative stability for the same range of $p$ and $n$: for sufficiently small $δ\ge 0$, every $n$-vertex triangle-free graph with bisection value at least the asymptotic optimum minus $δn^2$ is within $O_p(δn^2+n)$ edge edits of a complete bipartite graph with the optimal limiting class ratio.
A characterization of Griffiths semipositivity by top-degree optimal $\bar \partial$-estimates

We prove that a singular Hermitian metric $h$ on a vector bundle agrees almost everywhere with a Griffiths semipositive metric if its dual metric $h^*$ is locally integrable and the $\bar \partial$-equation admits solutions with optimal $L^2$-estimates for $(n,n)$-forms, where $n$ is the dimension of the base manifold. In particular, under this integrability assumption, Nakano semipositivity in the sense of optimal estimates implies Griffiths semipositivity.
On the group of automorphisms of the escaping sets of Hénon maps

In this article, we provide an explicit description of $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$, the group of automorphisms of the escaping set $I_H^+$ of a Hénon map that induce the identity on its fundamental group. More precisely, for a Hénon map $H(x,y)=(y,p(y)-δx),$ where $p$ is a polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$ and $δ\neq 0$, we show that $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$ is completely determined by the degree and the coefficients of $p$. Thus, the automorphism group of the escaping set, subject to the prescribed topological constraint, can be explicitly characterized in terms of the underlying Hénon map.
Kähler-Finsler rigidity of the Kobayashi metric and the Kähler base of weakly Kähler-Finsler metrics

In this paper, we establish a rigidity theorem: for every balanced, smooth, bounded pseudoconvex domain, its Kobayashi metric is a smooth, strongly pseudoconvex, Kähler-Finsler metric restricted on a neighborhood of the origin if and only if the domain is a Hermitian ellipsoid, biholomorphic to the unit ball. Thus for any balanced, smooth, bounded, strictly convex, and strongly pseudoconvex domain that is not biholomorphic to the unit ball, its Kobayashi metric is a non-Kähler-Finsler, weakly Kähler-Finsler metric. We also prove that the base manifold of every weak Kähler-Finsler metric is Kähler.
Global regularity and sharp decay rates for the one-dimensional hypo-viscous compressible Navier-Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces
Chen Liang; Zhaonan Luo; Zhaoyang Yin

In this paper, we study the global regularity of the one-dimensional hypo-viscous compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the critical Besov spaces, where the initial data are close to the constant equilibrium state. We introduce an effective velocity, constructed as a combination of the density and the velocity, which is used to capture the high-frequency behavior of $a$. By performing elaborate high-frequency and low-frequency estimates together with a bootstrap argument, we obtain global existence for $\frac{1}{2}\leβ<1$. In particular, when $\frac{1}{2}\leβ<\frac{3}{4}$, we also prove the uniqueness of solutions. Furthermore, under an additional low-frequency assumption, we establish the optimal time decay rates.
A double-logarithmic lifespan bound for axisymmetric Euler equations with a small initial swirl
Zijin Li; Xu Xiao; Linbin Yang

We study the axisymmetric incompressible Euler equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a small initial swirl. Fix $s>7/2$, and let $\boldsymbol{v}_0\in H^s(\mathbb{R}^3)$ be axisymmetric and divergence-free. If $\varepsilon=\|{\nabla\times(v_{0,θ}\boldsymbol{e}_θ)}\|_{L^\infty}$ is sufficiently small, then the lifespan $T_*$ of the corresponding $H^s$ solution satisfies $$ T_{*}\geq\frac{C_s}{1+\|{\boldsymbol{v}_0}\|_{H^s}} \left[ \log\log (\varepsilon^{-1}) \right]^{3/7}\,. $$ This removes the assumption by Danchin (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 141:1979-1993, 2013) that the domain must be distant from the axis of symmetry. Moreover, even for $\boldsymbol{v}_0\in H^3$, our result improves the fourfold iterated-logarithmic lower bound for the lifespan obtained by Li and Zhou (Z. Angew. Math. Phys. 75:219, 2024) to a threefold iterated-logarithmic bound.

In this paper, we study the extremal number of arborescences over orientations of a fixed graph. We prove that every alternating orientation of a plane Eulerian multigraph minimizes the rooted arborescence count among its Eulerian orientations. We also prove that every tournament of odd order maximizing the total number of arborescences is regular, and hence Eulerian. These results resolve Conjectures 5.1 and 5.4 of Bandekar et al. We further establish upper bounds for arborescence counts in orientations of complete bipartite graphs and characterize the orientations attaining them.
Two-step nilpotent Lie algebras obtained by quivers and geometric structures

In the study of geometric structures on nilmanifolds, two-step nilpotent Lie algebras obtained by graphs play an important role. Recently, additional examples of nilpotent Lie algebras have been constructed from finite quivers without cycles. These latter examples can have arbitrarily high degrees of nilpotency, and admit Riemannian Ricci soliton metrics. In this paper, we study nilpotent Lie algebras obtained by finite quivers without cycles that are two-step nilpotent, and we prove that they can also be obtained by graphs. Using this relationship, we demonstrate that every two-step nilpotent Lie algebra obtained by a finite quiver without cycles admits a pseudo-Riemannian Ricci-flat metric. Additionally, we also classify these nilpotent Lie algebras that admit symplectic structures.
Non-planar contact structures with Calabi-Yau Fillings and topological quantum computation

This paper is a non-planar counterpart of the author's earlier work on planar contact structures and topological quantum computation. On a planar page every branch point is paired by a liftable arc, and the pairing matches the Ising representation exactly, in that fixing the channels of the pairs already fixes the state. Here the page has genus g and connected binding, presented as a simple degree-three cover of the disk. Every maximal system of disjoint liftable arcs then has exactly g members and leaves two branch points unused, and the half-twist interchanging the two points is not liftable, although its cube is and lifts to the identity. Ising fusion does not see that leftover pair, determining its channel from the other g and acting there only by scalars, whereas Fibonacci fusion can leave the channel undetermined. The powers of the cube then act by ten distinct relative phases on a single joint eigenspace, while the Calabi-Yau Stein filling stays fixed. An integral residue criterion supplies the Calabi-Yau test, a factorization localized on a contact connected sum is automatically Calabi-Yau, and, unlike in the planar case, a Calabi-Yau factorization need not be the shortest.
Distributed Algorithm for Linear Least Squares Problems via Iteratively Preconditioning by Successive Over-Relaxation

This paper focuses on a novel distributed optimization algorithm for solving multi-agent linear least squares problems within a server-agent framework. Distributed methods are particularly suited to large-scale systems. The computational tasks can be partitioned across agents, while local data of one agent remain inaccessible to others. The proposed approach employs an iterative preconditioning scheme with the successive over-relaxation technique, leading to a substantial reduction of the number of iterations required for convergence, which presents a critical advantage where server-agent communication is costly. Theoretical convergence proof of the proposed algorithm is presented. Finally, benchmark problems are tested to demonstrate the performance comparison of the proposed approach over several prominent distributed methods.
Terao's freeness conjecture for arrangements of 15 and 16 lines

We prove that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of 15 and of 16 lines in the complex projective plane. Together with the theorem of Barakat and Kühne for at most 14 hyperplanes, this shows that freeness of a central arrangement of at most 16 planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$ is determined by its intersection lattice. The proof has a theoretical and a computational part. Combining published combinatorial criteria for freeness (due to Abe, Dimca, Dimca-Kühne-Pokora and Yoshinaga) with Bojanowski's Hirzebruch-type inequality and an elementary counting identity, we show that a counterexample would have exponents $(6,8)$ or $(7,7)$ for 15 lines and $(7,8)$ for 16 lines, and an intersection lattice subject to strong numerical constraints. We then enumerate all 22,544,280 simple rank 3 matroids satisfying these constraints, up to isomorphism, and determine the complex realization space of each of them exactly over $\mathbb{Q}$. Exactly eleven of them are realizable over $\mathbb{C}$, and on each of these the freeness of the realizations is constant. As a by-product we classify the free arrangements of 15 and 16 lines that are not divisionally free, have maximal multiplicity smaller than the smaller nontrivial exponent, and have at least four intersection points on every line.
Mixed Chern curvature on complete flags

We prove that the complete flag manifold SU(m)/T m-1, with m >= 3 and its standard complex structure, admits no invariant Hermitian metric with constant mixed Chern curvature when the coefficient of the holomorphic sectional curvature is nonzero. This extends the preceding nonexistence result for a particular Wallach metric on SU(3)/T2 to all invariant Hermitian metrics and to complete type-A flags of arbitrary dimension. Curvature evaluations on holomorphic root spheres contradict a necessary trace identity, covering both Kahler and non-Kahler invariant metrics and excluding both zero and nonzero curvature constants.
On Multi-label radio Labelings of Graphs

We propose and study a multi-labeling generalization of the $k$-radio labeling problem of graphs: given a graph $G$ and integers $k$ and $m$, assign to each vertex of $G$ a set of $m$ integer labels such that distinct labels assigned to a vertex differ by at least $k+1$, and the labels of any two distinct vertices $x$ and $y$ pairwise differ by at least $k+1-d(x,y)$, with $d(x,y)$ being the distance between vertices $x$ and $y$. We prove general bounds on the minimum span of such a labeling and more refined results for the case $k=1$. For paths and cycles, we derive sharp bounds on the minimum span when $k$ is small. We finally propose a conjecture for the minimum span on the path and for an almost-tight bound on the cycle.
Weak Limits of Parameter Estimation in Strongly Identifiable Mixture Models
Dung Le; Trang Pham; Alessandro Rinaldo; Nhat Ho

We study the asymptotic behavior of global maximum likelihood estimation in finite mixtures with an unknown number of components bounded by \(k\). Although convergence rates are well understood under strong identifiability, they do not determine the limiting distribution of mixing-measure loss. Under second-order strong identifiability, we establish two geometric results that connect density asymptotics to uncertainty about the mixing measure. First, we characterize the exact attainable density tangent set, accounting for the component budget shared by nonlocal vanishing components and local splitting directions. Second, we derive a sequential first-order expansion of squared Wasserstein loss, showing that its leading transportation cost is uniquely determined by the relative-density direction. Together with a Gaussian likelihood argmax theorem, these results yield joint weak convergence of the relative-density maximum likelihood estimator and \(\sqrt n W_2^2(\widehat G_n,G_*)\). The density limit maximizes a Gaussian likelihood process over the attainable tangent set, and the induced limit of \(n^{1/4}W_2(\widehat G_n,G_*)\) is generally non-Gaussian. We establish consistency of an \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) parametric bootstrap when \(m\to\infty\) and \(m/n\to0\). Numerical studies assess the approximation and distinguish bootstrap and optimization errors; a flow-cytometry application illustrates uncertainty summaries invariant to component labeling under a working mixture model.
The Exact Boundary of Linear Optimality in Witsenhausen's Counterexample

Witsenhausen's counterexample has resisted a closed form solution for decades. However, it has remained unknown whether a mathematically tractable representation exists or not. In this paper, we solve this open problem, showing that the optimal policies are either linear or not tame and characterizing the exact regions where the two properties hold. Moreover, in the linear optimal region, we give an essentially unique closed form solution for the optimal policy, and show that no optimal first-stage policy is definable in any $o$-minimal expansion of the ordered real field in the nonlinear optimal region.
Left tail asymptotics for the density of supercritical branching processes in random environment

Let $(Z_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a supercritical branching process in a random environment in which every individual produces at least one offspring, and let $W$ be the almost sure limit of the normalized $Z_n$. Write $p_1$ for the (random) probability that an individual has exactly one child and $m_0$ for the mean offspring number in a given environment. Assume that $p_1$ is positive almost surely and bounded away from $1$, that $m_0$ is bounded away from $1$ and from infinity together with a mild moment condition, and that $\log m_0$ is non-lattice. Let $a_0>0$ be the unique solution of the equation $\mathbb{E}[p_1 m_0^{a_0}]=1$. Under these assumptions, we determine the precise left tail asymptotics of the annealed law of $W$: the distribution function $F(x)=\mathbb{P}(W\leq x)$ satisfies $F(x)\sim D x^{a_0}$ as $x\downarrow 0$ with a constant $D\in(0,\infty)$ admitting an explicit representation, and the annealed density $w$ of $W$, which we show exists and can be chosen continuous on $(0,\infty)$, satisfies $w(x)\sim G x^{a_0-1}$ as $x\downarrow 0$ with $G=a_0 D>0$. These results extend the classical power-law left tail behavior of the martingale limit of a Galton--Watson process in the literature to the random environment setting, where the exponent $a_0$ is determined by the averaged environmental law rather than by a fixed offspring distribution.

We study Bass's finiteness problem for embeddings into proper quotients. Given a commutative ring R, a reduced finitely generated R-algebra A, and an ideal $J\triangleleft A$, we ask whether an R-algebra monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow_R A/J$ forces J=0. We give affirmative answers by presenting two arguments. Also, we discuss not only in the reduced case, but also in several non-reduced cases: when R is artinian and A is finite over R; when R is zero-dimensional and A is finite projective over R; and in a series of Cohen--Macaulay settings. In the module-theoretic direction, for a noetherian reduced ring, and a finitely generated, and torsion-free A-module M, we show that $M\hookrightarrow_R M/JM$ implies that J is contained in a minimal prime of A; if M is faithful, then J=0. Also, dual versions investigated. Examples illustrate the necessity of hypotheses.
Union of Translates of a Convex Body

Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a strictly convex body and let $Z\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set of sites in general position. We consider the problem of calculating the volume $μ_d$ of $\bigcup_{z\in Z}(z-K)$. Let $V_z$ be the Voronoi cell of $z\in Z$ with respect to the convex distance function induced by $K$, and let $N$ be the nerve of the Voronoi cells. When $K$ is a ball, a classical result reduces the inclusion-exclusion formula to a sum over $N$: $μ_d(\bigcup_{z\in Z}(z-K))=\sum_{J\in N}(-1)^{|J|+1}μ_d(\bigcap_{z\in J}(z-K))$. When may the hypothesis that $K$ is a ball be dropped? We show that for $d\leq 2$ the reduced formula holds for every strictly convex $K$, while for each $d\geq 3$ there is a strictly convex $K$ for which it fails. For $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, let $χ_x$ be the Euler characteristic of the subcomplex of $N$ induced by the sites lying in $K+x$. A sufficient condition for the reduced formula to hold is $χ_x\equiv 1$ on the union. When $d=3$ and $K$ is $C^4$, we show that $χ_x\equiv 1$ on the union for all $Z$ in general position if and only if $K$ is an ellipsoid. The proof relies on the Fubini-Pick affine invariant.
A New Proof of Wei's Theorem
Zhiqaing Wei; Mengyan Xing; Xingya Zhao

In the paper \emph{Structure and realizability for rational maps}, Wei proved the following. Let \(k\) nontrivial partitions of an integer \(d\ge 3\) be given, satisfying the Riemann--Hurwitz formula for the case of maps between two spheres. If \(k>\ell+1\), where \[ \ell=\min_i|π_i| \] is the shortest partition length, then there exists a rational map whose branch datum is given by these partitions. In this paper we give a new proof of Wei's theorem on realizing a tuple of partitions as the ramification data of a rational function. The proof is inductive on the shortest partition length. Two auxiliary results are established: a two-cut partition theorem and a gluing theorem for marked spherical coverings. These reduce any counterexample with shortest length \(\ell\ge3\) to auxiliary data with either fewer factors or smaller shortest length, while preserving the total defect and the marked conditions. The base case \(\ell\le2\) is quoted from the literature.
The global structure of bi-rotational self-expanders

We describe the self-expanders of the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{p+q+2}$ invariant under $O(p+1)\times O(q+1)$. Apart from the Clifford minimal cone, every such hypersurface is complete, proper and noncompact, and belongs to one of three families: two one-parameter families of embedded hypersurfaces diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{p+1}\times\mathbb{S}^{q}$ or to $\mathbb{R}^{q+1}\times\mathbb{S}^{p}$, whose profile curves leave an axis, and a two-parameter family diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{p}\times\mathbb{S}^{q}$, parametrized by the point of the profile curve closest to the origin, which is the generic family: its set of initial conditions is open and of full measure in the phase space. Every end is asymptotically conical, with explicit decay rates, and every such hypersurface has Euclidean volume growth. A profile curve of the third family has at most one loop, and the point of the curve closest to the origin lies on that loop.
The global structure of bi-rotational self-shrinkers

We describe the global structure of the self-shrinkers of the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{p+q+2}$ invariant under $O(p+1)\times O(q+1)$, without assuming properness or embeddedness. The main tool is a pair of piecewise monotone quantities along the profile curves, in the spirit of Hsiang's analysis of constant mean curvature hypersurfaces. We prove that every such self-shrinker other than the two invariant cylinders intersects both of them transversely, and all of them except the Clifford minimal cone are complete. Apart from those of the cylinders, each end is either asymptotic to a cone or meets both cylinders infinitely many times. Consequently, a complete noncompact example is proper if and only if all its ends are asymptotically conical, and this is equivalent to polynomial volume growth, to finite entropy, and to finitely many intersections with the cylinders. The reduced flow preserves a finite measure, and for almost every initial condition the profile curve is either closed or generates a complete nonproper self-shrinker of infinite entropy. We also bound the winding of the profile curve by its number of cylinder crossings and localize its self-intersections.
Random Clocks on Computation Paths]{Random Clocks on Computation Paths: How Far Can They Reach, and When Does Stepping Back Help?

We watch a computation only at moments chosen by a random clock that can leap ahead, pause, or step back, and we count looks rather than steps. How far can such a clock reliably see with polynomially many looks, and does stepping back help? Rare long leaps reach exponential and doubly exponential time, with infinitely many levels between polynomial and exponential time. A clock that tends to fall back sees only the start of the input, and below polynomial time we find infinitely many incomparable levels. Stepping back can help decisively. For clocks whose long leaps occur only at rare positions, no forward-only clock goes beyond polynomial time, while even single steps back raise the reach to exponential time. Stepping back cannot help, however, when the clock's leaps ignore its position.
A classification of the Nim-sequences for the two-element subtraction game with a single pass
In this paper, we provide a complete description of the preperiods, periodic lengths, and the Grundy-value sequences of two-element subtraction games with a single pass option.

Motzkin, Grünbaum, and Erdős and Purdy asked how many noncollinear blue points can coexist with $t$ red points in the real plane if every blue-spanned line contains a red point. We prove that there are at most $2.35t-3$ blue points, even over the complex numbers. For the complex higher-dimensional problem of Campbell, Kroeker, and Lund, we prove $b_k(t)\le1.40k^2t$. Colorings of cyclic Dowling geometries give a matching lower bound in order of magnitude for all $k\ge2$ and $t\ge3$. The planar proof uses frame normalization and a second-moment estimate; the higher-dimensional proof combines the degree bound of Kroeker and Lund with principal truncation.
Cohomological Milnor Fibrations of Landau--Ginzburg Models

We study the global topology of \emph{fundamentally tame} Landau--Ginzburg (LG) models on complete Kähler manifolds. We first show that the superpotential $f$ is surjective onto $\mathbb{C}$, then prove that $f$ restricts to a locally trivial fibration over the set of its regular values, which yields a global generalization of the classical Milnor fibration and provides an Ehresmann-type fibration in the non-proper setting. Assuming that $f$ has finitely many critical points, we use a Morse-theoretic argument to show that the relative homology of $\bigl(M,f^{-1}(c)\bigr)$, for a regular value $c$, is concentrated in the middle degree and has rank equal to the global Milnor number $μ_f$. We further identify the relative homotopy type of the fibers with that of the sublevel sets of $f$ at infinity.Finally, for deformations satisfying a uniform tameness condition on a Stein manifold, we construct the relative cohomology bundles at positive and negative infinity, each equipped with a natural flat Gauss--Manin connection.
Optimal Priors for Betting Tests with Bounded Payoffs: An Exact Efficiency Characterization

Testing by betting is a powerful framework that recasts hypothesis testing as a betting game. A popular approach uses an $F$-weighted portfolio with a predefined prior $F$. For suitable priors, this approach has recently been shown to achieve the optimal expected rejection time as the error probability goes to zero at a fixed alternative. Yet, the prior $F$ changes how the portfolio test behaves near the null. This motivates the question: Which prior should we use in testing-by-betting algorithms? We study bounded scalar payoffs and introduce an efficiency measure that allows the error probability and alternative to vary jointly. Under mild assumptions, we prove that efficiency equals a logarithmic decay index of the prior near zero. This gives a necessary and sufficient condition for optimality: Beta priors have infinite efficiency, whereas suitable Robbins-type priors attain efficiency 1. As an application, we consider testing a specified mean of a bounded random variable and describe an implementation of the portfolio algorithm with almost-linear computational complexity.
Classification of all non-split central extensions of naturally graded 2-filiform non-Lie Leibniz algebras

This paper deals with the naturally graded 2-filiform non-Lie Leibniz algebras over the field of complex numbers. There are two finite series of such algebras, defined in every dimension starting from five, and two further algebras which occur only in dimension five. For each of these algebras we classify, up to isomorphism, all of its non-split central extensions, of every possible dimension. The one-dimensional central extensions are already known from an earlier work, so the main part of the paper is devoted to the extensions of dimension two and higher. As usual, the classification is reduced to the description of the orbits of the automorphism group of the algebra on the subspaces of its second cohomology space with trivial coefficients. For each algebra and each dimension we give the complete list of these orbits together with the multiplication tables of the corresponding algebras, and we point out the extensions whose annihilator coincides with the added central ideal. Among the algebras obtained there are 2-filiform Leibniz algebras which are not naturally graded; this class of algebras has not been systematically studied so far.
Global weak solutions for a two-species Riesz cross-attraction system with quadratic diffusion

We establish global existence for a two-species cross-attraction system on $\mathbb R^3$, with quadratic diffusion and the common interaction operator $(-Δ)^{-s}$, where $1/2<s<1$. Nonnegative initial data in $L^1\cap L^\infty$ with finite second moments require no smallness condition on the masses. A joint energy and second-moment estimate and a coupled $L^p$ iteration give uniform a priori estimates for the regularized solutions. Compactness then yields mass-conserving global weak solutions, bounded on every finite time interval and strongly continuous in $L^1\cap L^2$. The energy inequality holds at every pair of time endpoints. Uniqueness and bounds uniform for all positive times are not asserted.
The multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality for chordal graphs
Shaohan Xu; Fengming Dong; Kexiang Xu

For a connected graph $G$, let $τ(G)$, $α(G)$ and $α^*(G)$ denote its numbers of spanning trees, acyclic orientations and totally cyclic orientations, respectively. We prove that $α(G)α^*(G)\geqτ(G)^2$ for every connected bridgeless chordal graph.
An intrinsic notion of visibility and classification of planar Denjoy-Wolff domains

In this article, we introduce an intrinsic notion of visibility with respect to the Kobayashi distance that does not require any boundary. We establish localization results for the Kobayashi distance on Kobayashi hyperbolic domains in $\mathbb{C}^d$ that satisfy this intrinsic visibility property. As an application of these localization results, we compare the Busemann horospheres of a domain with those of a subdomain. Recently, Benini and Bracci characterized simply connected planar domains with the Denjoy-Wolff property in terms of Busemann horospheres. More precisely, they proved that a proper simply connected planar domain has the Denjoy-Wolff property if and only if the closure of every Busemann horosphere meets the boundary of the domain in exactly one point. We introduce Condition (M$\star$), a condition of attaching a proper disk to the domain at a boundary point. Using our localization results together with this comparison of Busemann horospheres, we extend the characterization of Benini and Bracci to domains satisfying Condition (M$\star$) at every boundary point, and to domains satisfying it outside a totally disconnected subset of the boundary. In particular, we obtain a characterization for finitely connected domains and for a large class of infinitely connected domains having the Denjoy-Wolff property. These characterizations yield a variety of domains with the Denjoy-Wolff property, which we illustrate through example.
Quantitative stratification and optimal regularity for stationary $J$-holomorphic maps
Chang-Yu Guo; Ming-Lun Liu; Chang-You Wang

In this paper, we give an alternate proof of the $ε$-regularity theorem of Wang [Comm. Cont. Math. 2003] for weakly $J$-holomorphic maps by adapting the conservation law approach of Rivière [Invent. Math. 2007]. Then we adapt the powerful quantitative stratification method of Naber--Valtorta [Ann. Math. 2017] to obtain optimal volume estimates and rectifiability for the quantitative strata of stationary $J$-holomorphic maps. In contrast with general harmonic maps, the almost complex equation gives rise to an additional symmetry improvement: Every odd-dimensional translation symmetry extends to an even-dimensional one. Consequently, consecutive even and odd strata coincide, and the $k$-th quantitative stratum satisfies a tubular-neighborhood estimate with exponent $2m-2\lfloor k/2\rfloor$, where $2m$ is the real dimension of the domain. The corresponding strata are $2\lfloor k/2\rfloor$-rectifiable, with almost-everywhere unique complex planes of symmetry. Finally, we prove that every stationary $J$-holomorphic map is smooth if the target { manifold} admits no non-constant $J$-holomorphic sphere, improving the corresponding theorem of Wang.

We discuss rather basic problems on super principal bundles for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds (over $\mathbb{R}$) and analytic supermanifolds over a complete field of arbitrary characteristic. Sharper answers are obtained for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds and for homogeneous supermanifolds. Among others, it is proved for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds that given a $C^{\infty}$-supermanifold $B$ and a super Lie group $G$, there is a natural one-to-one correspondence (up to isomorphism) between the $G$-super principal bundles over $B$ and the $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$-principal bundles over $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$, where $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$ (resp., $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$) denotes the ordinary Lie group (resp., manifold) associated with $G$ (resp., $B$). To prove this, we show a generalized, equivariant version of the renowned Batchelor Theorem.
2-Local Derivations on Conformal Galilei Lie Algebras and Their Central Extensions

We classify 2-local derivations on the finite-dimensional conformal Galilei Lie algebras in three natural settings: the algebra without central extension, the mass central extension, and the exotic central extension. No additivity or linearity is assumed in the definition of a 2-local derivation. We prove that in every case each 2-local derivation is an ordinary derivation. For the unextended algebra, the proof combines characteristic-quotient normalization with separating vectors, invariant bilinear forms, rank-two mixed zero anchors, and a semisimple-perturbation argument for the standard module. For the mass central extension with $2\ell\ge3$, the residual map is first reduced to the center and then eliminated by a symplectic-anchor construction on the Heisenberg radical; a dimension argument in the centralizer of a regular semisimple element simultaneously handles singular reductive actions and the additional central shear that occurs in spatial dimension two. The endpoint $\ell=\tfrac12$ is the Schrödinger algebra; a self-contained symplectic-anchor proof includes all spatial dimensions, with explicit treatment of dimensions one and two. For the exotic extension, after center normalization we use conjugate middle-weight positions and an affine middle anchor to eliminate every central translate, including the one-sided middle-weight configurations. Consequently the set of 2-local derivations coincides with the derivation algebra for all admissible parameters, and hence every 2-local derivation in these families is automatically linear.
Semi-similar Prandtl Flows near a Stagnation Point: Dynamical Selection and Nonlinear Stability
Chen Gao; Tao Tao; Zhouping Xin; Shing-Tung Yau; Chuankai Zhao

This paper studies time-dependent semi-similar Prandtl flows with outer flow $U(x)=x^m$, where $m\geq1$. The normal coordinate is scaled by the local boundary-layer thickness, and time by the associated diffusion scale. Every time-monotone solution in the Oleinik class extends globally in time. The Falkner--Skan boundary layer globally attracts every such unsteady semi-similar profile. The convergence rate is exponential for $m=1$ and algebraic for $m>1$. We also prove nonlinear stability of each admissible time-dependent semi-similar trajectory under small compatible perturbations that break the semi-similar ansatz. Together, these results provide a dynamical justification of the time-dependent semi-similar class within the full Prandtl theory. For semi-similar flows, the Crocco transformation reduces the problem to a one-dimensional degenerate parabolic equation. Combined with weighted barriers, comparison principles propagate time monotonicity and lead to global continuation. Zero-order convergence and a one-sided gradient estimate then produce uniform strict concavity after a transient period; this concavity supplies the damping needed for derivative decay. The same damping mechanism extends to the full ultraparabolic perturbation equation, allowing us to close the nonlinear stability estimates.
The Maximum Commute Time of Regular Graphs
Jing Huang; Xuezhu Liao; Jiaxin Tang

For a connected simple regular graph $G$, let $τ(G)$ be the maximum commute time for simple random walk, and let $t_n$ be the maximum of $τ(G)$ over all such graphs of order $n$. Aldous and Fill conjectured that $t_n\sim3n^2/2$. We determine $t_n$ exactly and classify all maximizers for every even $n\geq10$ and every odd $n\geq15$; both thresholds are best possible. The maximizers are cubic block chains joined by bridges at even orders and quartic block chains joined at cut vertices at odd orders. The exact formulas specify the linear corrections according to the order modulo four and five, respectively, and imply $ t_n\sim \begin{cases} \dfrac32 n^2, & n\text{ even},\\[1mm] n^2, & n\text{ odd}, \end{cases} \qquad n\to\infty. $ Thus the conjectured asymptotic formula holds along even orders but fails along odd orders. The proof combines unit-current potential orderings, cut-current inequalities, and sharp block resistance bounds, supplemented by finite computations in exact rational arithmetic.
Finite BSC-Decomposition of Binary-Input Symmetric-Output Channels and Applications to Channel Simulation

We propose a finite BSC-decomposition method for representing an arbitrary binary-input symmetric-output channel (BISOC) as a mixture of binary symmetric channels (BSCs) with at most $\ell+1$ distinct crossover probabilities. We show that the weighted average capacity of the component BSCs exceeds the capacity of the original BISOC by at most $(π^2\log e)/(48\ell^2)+O(\ell^{-5/2})$ bits, and the leading term is asymptotically optimal in the worst case. Based on the finite BSC-decomposition, we design a channel simulation scheme for arbitrary BISOCs. Combined with efficient channel simulation algorithms for BSCs, our scheme achieves a communication rate with $O((\log n / n)^{2/3})$ redundancy over the capacity for simulating $n$ copies of a BISOC.
Carlo Francisco Adajar; Kevin J. McGown; Paul Pollack; Enrique Treviño

Following Johnson, Queen, and Sevilla, we call an order $\mathcal{O}$ in a number field $K$ \textsf{generalized Euclidean} if for all $α,β\in \mathcal{O}$ with $β\ne 0$ for which $α\mathcal{O}+β\mathcal{O}$ is a principal ideal of $\mathcal{O}$, there are $γ, ρ\in \mathcal{O}$ with $α=βγ+ ρ$ and $|N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(ρ)| < |N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(β)|$. We prove that only finitely many quadratic orders are generalized Euclidean. Additionally, assuming GRH, we show that for each fixed $d > 1$ there are only finitely many integers $m$ for which $T^d-m$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{Z}[m^{1/d}] = \mathbb{Z}[T]/(T^d-m)$ is generalized Euclidean. When $d$ is even, we can remove the assumption of GRH.
Asymptotic low slopes of toric exponential sums

Let $Δ$ be an integral Newton polytope containing the origin. We prove that the generic Newton slopes corresponding to Hodge slopes strictly smaller than one differ from their Hodge values by $O_Δ(p^{-1})$. No hypothesis is imposed on the semigroup generated by the lattice points of $Δ$. The proof combines an auxiliary prime and the Cartier operator to show that a coefficient of each required Dwork principal minor is nonzero. When the origin is interior to $Δ$, duality gives the same estimate for the corresponding high slopes and, in dimension two, for all slopes.
Computation of Free Boundary Minimal Tori via Extremal Steklov Eigenvalues

Fraser and Schoen showed that the first Steklov eigenfunctions of a metric maximizing the length-normalized first eigenvalue of a surface with boundary define a free boundary minimal immersion into a Euclidean ball. We develop a method for this extremal problem on surfaces of genus one with $b$ boundary components and use it to compute free boundary minimal tori for $b \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8\}$. By uniformization, the problem is a nonsmooth maximization over the modulus of a flat torus, the centers and radii of $b$ removed disks, and a boundary weight. The eigenvalues are computed with doubly periodic layer potentials, all derivatives follow from a single formula for the underlying pencil of boundary integral operators, and the coalescence of eigenvalues at a maximizer is handled by a two-stage nonsmooth method. The Lagrange multiplier matrix that certifies first-order stationarity rescales the eigenfunctions into the free boundary minimal immersion. For $b=1$, the supremum is the Fraser--Schoen bound $4π$, attained by branched double covers of the disk; the embedded torus with connected boundary of Carlotto, Franz, and Schulz is a saddle point, which answers their question whether it maximizes the eigenvalue in the negative. For $b \geq 2$ the largest values correspond to free boundary minimal tori in \mathbb{B}^5 and \mathbb{B}^6; the surfaces of Folha, Pacard, and Zolotareva, two disks joined by a central neck and $b$ equatorial necks, are maximizers within their symmetry class but saddle points of the full problem, with values increasing toward $4π$ as $b \to \infty$.
Self-Similar Solutions of the 2D Incompressible Euler Equations via a Lagrangian Construction
Thomas Y. Hou; Xiang Qin; Peicong Song; Wenhan Zhang

We give a Lagrangian construction of forward self-similar solutions of the $2$D incompressible Euler equation. For every $1<α<2$ and every real $h\in L^{2/α}(\mathbb{S}^1)$, the construction produces a flow with initial vorticity $|x|^{-α}h(\arg x)$, without smallness or sign assumptions. The argument is based on a fixed-point formulation of backward particle transport from time $t=1$ to $t=0$. Mollifying the Biot--Savart velocity in self-similar variables preserves exact vorticity transport, while symmetrization yields the unforced Euler equation in velocity form even when the ordinary vorticity flux is not locally integrable. The limiting solution admits an almost-everywhere invertible, measure-preserving regular Lagrangian flow from time zero, with strong local continuity and preservation of signed value distributions and absolutely integrable Casimirs.
Convergence of alternating score-system iterations for regularized Landau particle dynamics
Yeoneung Kim; Donghyun Lee; Sung-Jun Son

We analyze an alternating iteration for score-based particle approximations of the homogeneous Landau equation. Each step computes a regularized score along the previous trajectory and recomputes the trajectory with that score frozen. First, at fixed positive regularization, we prove existence, uniqueness, and $W_1$-Lipschitz stability of a Tikhonov score minimizer in a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space embedded in $C_b^2$. For bounded Lipschitz collision matrices, this yields factorial convergence to the coupled regularized dynamics on every finite interval, with constants independent of particle number. Global objective gaps and system residuals control inexact solves, and structural kernel assumptions ensure momentum and energy conservation. The mean-field and alternating-iteration limits commute at fixed regularization in this regime. Second, score-difference cancellation extends the theory to far-field-truncated Landau kernels with $γ\geq -2$ and the uncut case $γ=-2$. For the uncut three-dimensional Coulomb kernel, a separate continuum construction gives local factorial convergence from bounded, compactly supported densities. Third, we characterize the obstruction to removing regularization at fixed particle number and establish a separate conditional density-level convergence criterion under uniform regularity and approximation assumptions, using relative entropy. A heat-equation counterexample shows that an unregularized density-level Picard iteration can diverge. Atomic Coulomb and simultaneous particle-zero-regularization limits remain open.
Free abelian group actions on projective fibered varieties

Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional normal projective variety of Kodaira dimension $κ$ and $G$ an abelian subgroup of automorphisms such that all elements of $G\backslash \{\mathrm{id}\}$ are of positive entropy. Dinh and Sibony showed that $G$ is actually free abelian of rank $\le n-κ-1$. In this paper, we show that after replacing $G$ by a finite-index subgroup, there exists a G-Equivariant Minimal Model Program for the pair $(X, G)$ when $\mathrm{rank}(G)=n-κ-1$ and $κ>0$, and the very general fiber of the final model is a klt Calabi-Yau surface or a $Q$-abelian variety provided that the termination of flips holds in this setting.
A Fourier expansion principle for coherent cohomology of powers of Tate curves

In the case of the totally degenerate split degenerations given by fibered powers of Tate curves over $\mathbf{Z}[[q^{1/w}]]$, this article proves a Fourier expansion principle that applies to higher coherent (equivariant) cohomology classes of rigidified line bundles on the $\mathbf{Z}((q^{1/w}))$-fiber. We do not require any ampleness hypotheses. This generalizes a previous Fourier expansion principle due to Faltings--Chai that applies only to sections of ample line bundles; that version was used as a key step in their proof of their classification of polarized degenerations and thus in the construction of toroidal compactifications of moduli spaces of polarized abelian varieties. This article can be considered as a theory of Fourier expansions for algebraic theta cocycles associated to possibly indefinite quadratic forms, and has application to arithmetic: in joint work with Venkatesh, we have used it to produce an algebraic theory of Kudla--Millson indefinite modular theta functions.
Lusztig's asymptotic algebra and a cell factorisation for the second lowest two-sided cell in type $\tilde{B}_n$

We determine Lusztig's asymptotic algebra for the second lowest two-sided cell~$Δ_1$ in the equal parameter extended affine Weyl group $\tilde{\mathsf{B}}_n$ for all $n\geq 2$, realising it as a full matrix algebra over the representation ring of $\mathsf{Sp}_{2n-2}(\CC)\times C_2$ with $C_2$ the group of order~$2$. Our result is an explicit isomorphism of based rings, determining the image of each basis element $\mathsf{t}_w$ of the asymptotic algebra. As a consequence we verify that Lusztig's original conjecture from 1989 on the structure of the asymptotic algebra holds for this cell. A key ingredient in our proof is a refinement of Shi's description of~$Δ_1$, giving an explicit parametrisation of the elements of this cell (a \textit{cell factorisation}). This cell factorisation simultaneously describes all intersections of left and right cells, with uniqueness and length-additivity of expressions. Applications include a classification of the involutions in $Δ_1$, and a calculation of the length generating functions for $Δ_1$ and the right cells in~$Δ_1$.
Jumps and Iterated Jumps of Perfect Subtrees of Positive Trees

An infinite (binary) tree is \emph{positive} iff its set of paths is non-null. As an elementary observation, positives trees always have positive perfect subtrees. Given a positive tree of certain complexity, here we present several theorems concerning the distribution of the Turing jumps or iterated Turing jumps of (positive) perfect subtrees of the given tree in the universe of Turing degrees.

Using the Hadamard matrix for dimension reduction can accelerate the computation due to the fast Hadamard transform. However, the previous target dimension bounds in terms of the Gaussian width depend on the ambient dimension. In this paper, we obtain the following ambient dimension free bound using three Hadamard-diagonal blocks. Let $H\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be the normalized Walsh-Hadamard matrix, and let $D_1,D_2,D_3\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be independent Rademacher diagonal matrices. We prove that for any symmetric set $T\subset \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, \[ \mathbb P\left\{\sup_{\boldsymbol t\in T}\big|\frac dm\|P_ΩHD_3HD_2HD_1\boldsymbol t\|_2^2-1\big|\le\varepsilon\right\} \ge1-δ\] whenever \[ m\gtrsim\varepsilon^{-2}w(T)^2\log^2\frac eδ\,\log^4\!\left(e+\frac{w(T)}\varepsilon\log\frac eδ\right). \] Here $w(T)$ is the Gaussian width of $T$, and $Ω$ is a set of $m$ distinct coordinates chosen uniformly. This is the first ambient dimension free bound on the target dimension using Hadamard transforms, for an arbitrary symmetric set in terms of its Gaussian width. We also prove that it is impossible to obtain an ambient dimension free bound for an arbitrary set in terms of its Gaussian width using two Hadamard-diagonal blocks.
Noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for convolution operators under $L_1$-Hörmander conditions
Guixiang Hong; Liang Wang; Xumin Wang; Bang Xu

We prove weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for families of scalar convolution operators acting on operator-valued function spaces. A joint $L_1$-Hörmander condition, together with a maximal strong type estimate at one exponent $1<r\leq\infty$, suffices. The kernels may be complex-valued and need not have uniformly bounded $L_1$ norms. Under a size condition, the result also yields a weak endpoint estimate for all sharp truncation radii of singular kernels. This resolves, for convolution kernels, the problem mentioned in \cite[Remark~5.5]{parcet09pseudo} and recalled in Parcet's recent survey \cite[Remark~1.3]{Parcet2026ICM}. The proof involves not only a simultaneous dyadic representation of the operators but also a noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates of the resulting dyadic operators. This approach seems entirely new even in the commutative setting. Numerous applications are provided. On the one hand, it yields various maximal inequalities and pointwise convergence results for integrable kernels and dyadic approximations of the identity, monotone $L\log L$ majorants, and Poisson integrals on nilpotent groups and symmetric spaces. On the other hand, via various transference techniques, it implies maximal inequalities for Fourier multipliers, Schur multipliers and double operator integrals, together with bilateral almost uniform convergence of dyadic Fourier summation methods on $L_1$ of group von Neumann algebras.
A Benders decomposition approach for hierarchical k-medoids

We study a hierarchical clustering problem formulated as a sum of k-medoids objectives. This problem is related to the multi-period p-median problem, but instead of having nested facilities, we consider a hierarchy of nested assignments. We present two Benders formulations from the p-median literature and show how the obtained nested p-median solutions can be converted into hierarchical k-medoids solutions. We validate our methods on various instances. First, we show on small-scale instances that a standard Benders decomposition approach achieves speedups of up to three orders of magnitude over an existing branch-and-price method, while producing hierarchical k-medoids solutions that are at most 5% away from optimality. Second, we present an aggregated Benders heuristic that can handle instances with more than 13,000 observations.
On one-dimensional pressureless Euler--Poisson systems: existence for non-semiconvex interaction potentials
Andrew Xie; Emmanuel Alayande; Christopher Chun; Yusen Li; Rohan Mawalkar; Adrian Tudorascu; Adam Van

One-dimensional Euler-Poisson-type systems with interaction potentials that are repulsive at short range and attractive at long range are useful simplified models that describe biological aggregation. In the current work we employ new techniques to treat compactly supported solutions in the case where the potential is $C^1$ and satisfies certain coercivity growth conditions although it is not necessarily semiconvex, as required in previous work. Central to this approach are uniform bounds on the positions and velocities of discrete sticky-particle solutions to such a system, which requires the potential be only $C^{0, 1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. In the semiconvex case, these bounds also yield convergence of time-shifted trajectories to an eternal solution. The tradeoff, just as in the case of repulsive Euler-Poisson, is that we cannot claim that the emerging solutions for non-semiconvex potentials are sticky.
On the Hausdorff dimension of oscillatory motions in three-body problems

We show that for the Sitnikov example and for the restricted planar circular 3-body problem the set of oscillatory motions often has maximal Hausdorff dimension. Also, we construct Newhouse domains for both problems.
Berry--Esseen Bounds for High-Temperature Ising Models
